spotters.answer: Choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle, formed by tela choroidea invaginating along the choroid fissure between the fornix and the thalamus. Its cuboidal ependymal cells with tight junctions form the blood cerebrospinal fluid barrier and secrete around 500 ml of cerebrospinal fluid a day. It is bulkiest at the atrium as the glomus, where it commonly calcifies.
spotters.followup: Name the arteries supplying this plexus and state which parts of the ventricle contain no plexus.

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned part of the brainstem and name the cranial nerves arising from it.
spotters.answer: Midbrain or mesencephalon, connecting pons to diencephalon, consisting of tectum, tegmentum and the crus cerebri, with the substantia nigra between tegmentum and crus. The oculomotor nerve emerges into the interpeduncular fossa and the trochlear nerve from the dorsal surface below the inferior colliculus. It is traversed by the cerebral aqueduct.
spotters.followup: Describe Weber syndrome: which artery, which structures, which signs?

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned column of fibres and state the tracts it carries.
spotters.answer: Peduncle of the midbrain, the crus cerebri, carrying corticospinal and corticonuclear fibres in its middle three fifths, frontopontine fibres medially and parieto temporo occipitopontine fibres laterally. The oculomotor nerve emerges on its medial side into the interpeduncular fossa. In uncal herniation the opposite peduncle is pushed against the tentorial edge, the Kernohan notch, giving ipsilateral hemiparesis as a false localising sign.
spotters.followup: Which structure lies immediately dorsal to this bundle, and which pigment does it contain?

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned part of the brainstem and name the cranial nerves related to it.
spotters.answer: Pons, lying between midbrain and medulla oblongata, with a basilar part of transverse pontocerebellar fibres and a dorsal tegmentum forming the upper half of the floor of the fourth ventricle. The trigeminal nerve emerges from its lateral surface, and the abducent, facial and vestibulocochlear nerves at the pontomedullary junction. It is supplied by pontine branches of the basilar artery, and basilar occlusion may give locked in syndrome.
spotters.followup: Explain why central pontine myelinolysis follows rapid correction of hyponatraemia and what signs it produces.

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned part of the brainstem and state one clinical syndrome affecting it.
spotters.answer: Medulla oblongata, extending from the pontomedullary junction to the level of the foramen magnum, showing the pyramids, the decussation of the pyramids, the olives and the roots of the glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory and hypoglossal nerves. It contains the cardiovascular and respiratory centres. Occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery produces the lateral medullary syndrome of Wallenberg.
spotters.followup: List the signs of Wallenberg syndrome and explain the dissociated sensory loss.

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned structure and state its arterial supply and the side of its signs.
spotters.answer: Cerebellum, occupying the posterior cranial fossa behind the pons and medulla oblongata and below the tentorium cerebelli, connected to the brainstem by three peduncles. It is supplied by the superior cerebellar, anterior inferior cerebellar and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries. Hemispheric lesions cause ipsilateral signs: intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, dysmetria, nystagmus and hypotonia.
spotters.followup: Why are cerebellar signs ipsilateral? Trace the double decussation involved.

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned dural fold and state its attachments and clinical importance.
spotters.answer: Tentorium cerebelli, a crescentic fold of dura roofing the posterior cranial fossa and separating the occipital lobe from the cerebellum. Its attached margin runs along the transverse sulci and the superior border of the petrous temporal bone to the posterior clinoid process, and its free margin bounds the tentorial notch which transmits the midbrain. Herniation of the uncus through this notch compresses the oculomotor nerve and the peduncle of the midbrain.
spotters.followup: Which dural venous sinuses lie in the attached and free margins of this fold?

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned artery and state its territory.
spotters.answer: Anterior cerebral artery, arising from the internal carotid artery, running above the optic nerve to the longitudinal fissure, where the two vessels are joined by the anterior communicating artery. It supplies the medial surface of the hemisphere as far back as the parieto occipital sulcus and a strip over the superomedial border. Occlusion beyond the communicating artery causes contralateral weakness and sensory loss maximal in the leg, with urinary incontinence and grasp reflex.
distractors: sphenoid part of middle cerebral artery
precommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
insular part of middle cerebral artery
spotters.followup: Name the perforating branch of this artery that supplies the head of the caudate nucleus and the deficit its occlusion causes.
spotters.sub: Cerebral arterial circle and medial surface

spotters.target: sphenoid part of middle cerebral artery
spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned arterial segment and state the branches arising from it.
spotters.answer: Sphenoid or M1 part of the middle cerebral artery, running laterally in the stem of the lateral sulcus behind the lesser wing of the sphenoid to the limen insulae. It gives the medial and lateral lenticulostriate perforators to the internal capsule, putamen, globus pallidus and caudate nucleus. Occlusion proximal to these branches gives a dense contralateral hemiplegia affecting face, arm and leg equally, unlike a cortical branch occlusion.
distractors: insular part of middle cerebral artery
spotters.followup: Which of these perforators is called the artery of cerebral haemorrhage, and which structure does it most often bleed into?
spotters.sub: Cerebral arterial supply, base of brain

spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned artery and name the syndrome caused by its occlusion.
spotters.answer: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery, the largest branch of the vertebral artery, winding around the medulla oblongata between the roots of the glossopharyngeal, vagus and accessory nerves to reach the inferior surface of the cerebellum. It supplies the dorsolateral medulla, the inferior vermis and the choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle. Occlusion, often actually of the vertebral artery, causes the lateral medullary syndrome of Wallenberg.
distractors: postcommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
precommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
spotters.followup: Why is there ipsilateral facial pain loss with contralateral body pain loss in this syndrome?

spotters.target: postcommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
spotters.prompt: Identify the pinned arterial segment and state its cortical territory.
spotters.answer: Postcommunicating or P2 part of the posterior cerebral artery, running distal to the junction with the posterior communicating artery, winding round the peduncle of the midbrain in the ambient cistern above the tentorial edge. It supplies the inferior surface of the temporal lobe and the occipital lobe including the visual cortex, and gives the splenial artery to the splenium of the corpus callosum. Occlusion produces contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.
distractors: precommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
spotters.followup: Which nerve is compressed when this artery is displaced downwards in uncal herniation, and which segment gives the thalamoperforating branches?
spotters.sub: Cerebral arterial circle, around the midbrain

competencies.statement: Describe the general features and functions of bones, and identify these features on bones of the upper limb.
competencies.note: Code AN1.1 and its subject (general features of bone) are reconstructed from memory of the NMC CBME 2019 Anatomy document, not quoted verbatim. My wording is a paraphrase. The topic heading 'General anatomy' is confident; the exact sub-number is high confidence but not quoted.

competencies.statement: Classify bones as long, short, flat, irregular, pneumatic and sesamoid, with examples from the upper limb.
competencies.note: Reconstructed from memory, not quoted. Pisiform is the sesamoid example and clavicle the atypical long bone; both exist in the model. No pneumatic bone exists in this block, so that class can only be named, not shown.

competencies.statement: Describe the blood supply of a long bone and the concept of nutrient and periosteal supply.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed from memory. Honest limitation: the model has no named nutrient arteries or periosteum. This competency can only be demonstrated by pairing each long bone with the parent trunk from which its nutrient branch arises, which is an inference the teacher must state aloud.

competencies.statement: Explain the terms diaphysis, epiphysis, metaphysis, epiphyseal plate and growing end, and identify them on upper limb long bones.
competencies.note: Reconstructed from memory. I am moderately confident this sits at AN1.4 or AN1.5; departments using a different print should re-map the sub-number. The model geometry is adult bone, so the epiphyseal plate itself is not a separate mesh: regions are pointed out on the whole-bone mesh.

competencies.statement: Describe the classification of muscle by shape and fibre architecture and identify examples of each on the upper limb.
competencies.note: Code AN2.1 and the wording are reconstructed from memory, not quoted. Deltoid is the multipennate example and is present only as three named parts, which is actually convenient for teaching its three fibre directions.

competencies.statement: Describe the general structure of arteries and veins and distinguish them by wall, lumen and course on named upper limb vessels.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed from memory. The model pairs venae comitantes with their arteries (radial artery and radial vein, ulnar artery and ulnar vein), which makes the artery versus vein contrast directly demonstrable.

competencies.statement: Explain the terms anastomosis, collateral circulation and end artery, and demonstrate arterial anastomoses of the upper limb.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed from memory. This is the strongest general anatomy competency in this model: the elbow anastomosis is present as four named recurrent and collateral vessels plus both parent trunks, and the palmar arches are complete.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, serratus anterior and subclavius.
competencies.note: Code AN7.1 and the muscle list are reconstructed from memory of the CBME pectoral region topic, not quoted. Nerve supply cannot be shown: the model contains no pectoral, long thoracic or nerve to subclavius geometry, so that half of the competency is spoken, not pinned.

competencies.statement: Explain the anatomical basis of winging of the scapula.
competencies.note: The sub-number is uncertain: I am reconstructing this as AN7.5, and some prints place winging of scapula at AN7.6 or under the axilla topic. The long thoracic nerve is absent from the model, so the lesion is taught through the muscle and its scapular attachment, with the antagonist scapular retractors shown for contrast.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the boundaries, walls and contents of the axilla.
competencies.note: Code AN8.1 and wording reconstructed from memory. Latissimus dorsi is absent from this model, so the posterior wall is incomplete and must be flagged to students. Axillary lymph nodes and the brachial plexus are also absent, so contents are limited to the vessels.

competencies.statement: Describe the extent, parts, relations and branches of the axillary artery.
competencies.note: Sub-number uncertain. I am reconstructing the axillary artery competency as AN8.2, but in some prints AN8.2 is the brachial plexus and the artery sits at AN8.3 or AN8.4. Departments should re-map against their own scheme. Note the model has no subscapular artery trunk or lateral thoracic artery: circumflex scapular artery is present without its parent, and the three-part division must be taught using pectoralis minor as the landmark.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles connecting the upper limb to the vertebral column.
competencies.note: Code AN9.1 reconstructed from memory. Latissimus dorsi is absent from the model, which is a real gap in this competency and should be declared. Trapezius exists only as three named parts, which suits teaching its three actions on the scapula separately. Accessory nerve and dorsal scapular nerve are absent.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of deltoid and the muscles of the rotator cuff.
competencies.note: Code AN10.1 reconstructed from memory. Structure names copied exactly, including the inconsistency in the model list where infraspinatus carries the word muscle and supraspinatus does not. All four cuff muscles are present, so this competency maps cleanly. Nerve supply is spoken only.

competencies.statement: Describe the arterial anastomosis around the scapula and explain its significance in obstruction of the axillary artery.
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed, likely AN10.2 or AN10.3. Wording is my paraphrase. All three limbs of the scapular anastomosis exist as separate meshes, which is unusual and makes this one of the best supported applied competencies in the block. The subscapular artery trunk itself is absent.

competencies.statement: Explain the anatomical basis of injury to the axillary nerve and the posterior circumflex humeral vessels in fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus and in shoulder dislocation.
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed and uncertain. The axillary nerve does not exist in this model, so the quadrangular space contents can only be shown as the posterior circumflex humeral artery plus the boundary muscles, with the nerve described verbally alongside its artery. Denervation is demonstrated on deltoid and teres minor.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the anterior and posterior compartments of the arm.
competencies.note: Code AN11.1 reconstructed from memory. Serious and declarable gap: biceps brachii and triceps brachii are both absent from this model, so the two principal muscles of the competency cannot be shown. What remains is brachialis and coracobrachialis in front and anconeus behind. A department should treat this competency as only partially supported.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the boundaries and contents of the cubital fossa.
competencies.note: Code AN11.2 reconstructed from memory. Pronator teres is absent, so the medial boundary is missing and must be stated. The biceps tendon and median nerve are also absent. The floor (brachialis and supinator) and the arterial contents are complete.

competencies.statement: Describe the formation, course and termination of the superficial veins of the upper limb and explain the anatomical basis of venepuncture at the cubital fossa.
competencies.topic: Superficial venous drainage of the upper limb
competencies.note: Code is the least certain in this map. I am reconstructing it as AN11.5, but the superficial veins and venepuncture competency appears under the forearm and hand topic (around AN12.9 to AN12.11) in some prints of the CBME document. The anatomy itself maps completely: the whole superficial chain from the dorsal venous network to the axillary vein exists as separate meshes.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the anterior compartment of the forearm.
competencies.note: Code AN12.1 reconstructed from memory. Two flexors are absent from the model and must be declared: pronator teres and flexor carpi ulnaris. The remaining superficial, intermediate and deep flexors are all present, so the layered dissection sequence can still be taught.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the posterior compartment of the forearm.
competencies.note: Code AN12.2 reconstructed from memory. This is the most completely supported competency in the block: every superficial and deep extensor including the three outcropping thumb muscles is present. Caution for content authors: the upper limb list also contains an entry named extensor digitorum longus, which is a lower limb muscle name and should not be used here.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the intrinsic muscles of the hand.
structures: flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand
set of palmar interossei of hand
set of dorsal interossei of hand
competencies.note: Code AN12.3 reconstructed from memory. Adductor pollicis is absent. Lumbricals and interossei exist only as grouped meshes (set of), so individual first to fourth identification is not possible; test them as functional groups. Note the list also carries opponens digiti minimi of foot, which must not be used in upper limb content.

competencies.statement: Describe the formation, completion and branches of the superficial and deep palmar arterial arches and their surface relations.
structures: proper palmar digital vein of little finger
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed, likely AN12.4 or AN12.5. Both arterial arches, their two parent trunks and princeps pollicis are present, so arch formation and dominance are fully demonstrable. Common and proper palmar digital arteries are absent, so the digital branching is shown only on the venous side.

competencies.statement: Explain the anatomical basis of carpal tunnel syndrome.
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed and uncertain. Major limitation to declare: neither the flexor retinaculum nor the median nerve exists in this model, so the tunnel roof and its compressed content cannot be pinned. What can be shown is the carpal arch floor (the four boundary bones at each end), the nine tendons that pass through, and the thenar muscles that waste. Use it as a bony boundaries exercise, not a nerve compression exercise.

competencies.statement: Explain the anatomical basis of claw hand following ulnar nerve injury.
structures: set of palmar interossei of hand
set of dorsal interossei of hand
flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed and uncertain. The ulnar nerve is absent, so the lesion is taught through its territory: the hypothenar group, the interossei and the medial two lumbricals, with the ulnar artery and the pisohamate landmarks marking the nerve's course at the wrist. Because lumbricals are a single grouped mesh, the medial two cannot be isolated to explain the ulnar paradox.

competencies.statement: Describe the boundaries, floor and contents of the anatomical snuff box and explain its clinical importance.
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed. Both boundaries, the floor bones, the radial artery in the floor and the cephalic vein crossing the roof are all present, so this maps completely apart from the styloid process being part of the whole radius mesh rather than a separate pinnable feature.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the type, articulating surfaces, capsule, ligaments, movements, muscles producing movements and blood supply of the shoulder joint.
competencies.note: Code AN13.1 reconstructed from memory; the CBME joints competency is written as one statement covering shoulder, elbow, wrist and first carpometacarpal joints, and I have split it into three rows so each maps to its own structures. Capsule, glenoid labrum and the glenohumeral and coracoacromial ligaments are absent from the model, so articulating surfaces, muscles and blood supply are demonstrable but the ligamentous stability is not.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the type, articulating surfaces, movements and muscles producing movements at the elbow and the superior and inferior radio-ulnar joints.
competencies.note: Reconstructed sub-number, split from the composite AN13 joints competency as noted above. Pronation and supination map well: supinator, pronator quadratus and the interosseous membrane are all present. Biceps brachii and triceps brachii are absent, so the principal flexor and the sole extensor of the elbow cannot be shown. Annular and collateral ligaments are absent.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the type, articulating surfaces and movements of the wrist joint, the intercarpal joints and the first carpometacarpal joint.
competencies.note: Reconstructed sub-number, split from the composite AN13 joints competency. All eight carpal bones are individually present, so the two carpal rows, the radiocarpal articulation and the saddle joint at the thumb base are fully demonstrable. This is the strongest osteology mapping in the block. Ligaments and the articular disc are absent.

competencies.statement: Explain the anatomical basis of fracture of the scaphoid and the resulting avascular necrosis of its proximal fragment.
competencies.topic: Joints and osteology of the hand: applied anatomy
competencies.note: Sub-number reconstructed and uncertain; some prints place scaphoid fracture under the hand topic rather than under joints. The dorsal carpal branch that supplies the scaphoid is not a separate mesh, so the retrograde blood supply must be described verbally while pointing at the radial artery in the snuff box floor and the scaphoid itself.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts, features and side determination of the bones of the lower limb: femur, patella, tibia and fibula.
competencies.topic: Osteology of the thigh and leg
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed from memory, not quoted. I am confident the CBME lower limb block sits somewhere in the AN14 to AN21 range and that the verb pair used is 'Describe and identify' for osteology items, but I cannot verify the exact numeral or sub-numeral. The official competency also asks for the hip bone, which this model does not contain.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the tarsal bones, metatarsals and phalanges of the foot and their articulations.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed, not quoted. The model carries all seven tarsals, all five metatarsals, the full phalangeal set and a sesamoid, so this competency is fully anchorable. I have listed a representative twelve because of the cap; metatarsals two, three and four and the remaining phalanges also exist in the model.

competencies.statement: Describe the fascia lata, the iliotibial tract and the saphenous opening, and demonstrate their relations.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed, not quoted. Partial anchor only, and a department should know why: the model has the iliotibial tract as geometry but has no fascia lata sheet, no cribriform fascia and no saphenous opening margin, so the saphenous opening can only be inferred from the point where great saphenous vein meets femoral vein.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the anterior compartment of the thigh.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed. The stem 'Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the ... compartment' is the standard CBME phrasing pattern and I am reproducing it from memory rather than quoting a verified line. The nerve supply half of this competency cannot be demonstrated on this model: there is no femoral nerve. Iliopsoas is also absent, so the compartment shown is quadriceps plus sartorius only.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the boundaries, floor, roof and contents of the femoral triangle, including the femoral sheath and its compartments.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Anchors well on the vascular contents and two of the three muscular boundaries. Missing from the model and therefore not demonstrable: the inguinal ligament (superior boundary), the femoral nerve, the femoral sheath and canal, the deep inguinal lymph nodes, iliopsoas, and the profunda femoris artery itself, although the deep femoral vein is present and can stand in for the position of the artery.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the boundaries and contents of the adductor canal.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Good anchor: all three walls and both vessels exist, and the descending genicular artery lets a student see the terminal branch given off in the canal. Not demonstrable: the saphenous nerve, the nerve to vastus medialis, and the adductor hiatus as a defined opening.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the medial compartment of the thigh, and describe the course of the obturator nerve.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Muscle half anchors completely, and unusually the model separates adductor minimus, which most atlases fold into adductor magnus. The obturator nerve half of the competency cannot be shown at all: no nerves exist in this model.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the gluteal region.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Strongest anchor in the block: every gluteal muscle including the short lateral rotator set is present. Attachments can only be shown on the femur, since the hip bone and sacrum are not in this region's geometry, so proximal attachments must be described rather than pinned.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the structures passing above and below the piriformis and their relations in the gluteal region.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. This is a deliberately reduced version of the official competency. The structures the competency is really about, the sciatic nerve, superior and inferior gluteal vessels and nerves, pudendal nerve and posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, are all absent. What can honestly be taught here is the muscular key: piriformis as the landmark and the layered order of the short rotators below it.

competencies.statement: Demonstrate the safe site for intramuscular injection in the gluteal region and explain the anatomical basis for choosing it.
competencies.topic: Applied anatomy of the gluteal region
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Included because it is a high-yield applied competency and the muscular target, the upper outer quadrant over gluteus medius and minimus, is fully present. The structure the student is avoiding, the sciatic nerve, is not in the model, so the risk half must be described verbally against the position of piriformis and the greater trochanter of the femur.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the posterior compartment of the thigh.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Flag for the department: biceps femoris is NOT in this model, so the hamstring group is incomplete and this competency cannot be signed off on the model alone. What it does support well is the hamstring part of adductor magnus and the pes anserinus, since sartorius, gracilis and semitendinosus are all present and insert on the tibia.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the boundaries, roof, floor and contents of the popliteal fossa.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Vascular contents anchor completely, including all five genicular branches, which is better coverage than most plastic models give. Missing: biceps femoris and both heads of gastrocnemius, which means three of the four boundaries are incomplete, plus the tibial and common fibular nerves and the popliteal lymph nodes.

competencies.statement: Describe the arterial anastomosis around the knee joint and name its contributing vessels.
competencies.topic: Arterial anastomoses of the lower limb
structures: descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. This is the single best-served competency in the block: every named contributor to the genicular anastomosis exists as separate geometry, including the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery and the anterior tibial recurrent artery. The only usual contributor missing is the circumflex fibular artery.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the anterior compartment of the leg and the course of the anterior tibial vessels.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Compartment is incomplete: extensor digitorum longus is absent from the model, so three of the four anterior compartment muscles are shown. The deep fibular nerve, which the official competency requires, is absent. The interosseous membrane of the leg is present, which lets the compartment boundary be shown properly.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, nerve supply and actions of the muscles of the lateral compartment of the leg and trace the tendon of fibularis longus into the sole.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Anchors well, and the tendon course is genuinely traceable here because the model contains the long plantar ligament and the cuboid groove landmark plus both fibularis longus and brevis insertions. The superficial fibular nerve is absent.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the structures on the dorsum of the foot, including the dorsalis pedis artery, the dorsal venous arch and the extensor tendons.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Vascular anatomy of the dorsum is well represented down to digital level. Missing: extensor digitorum longus and extensor digitorum brevis, the extensor retinacula, and the deep fibular nerve, so the tendon fan across the dorsum is only partly shown.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments and actions of the muscles of the superficial posterior compartment of the leg and the formation of the calcaneal tendon.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Significant gap the department must know about: gastrocnemius is NOT in this model. Soleus, plantaris and the calcaneal tendon itself are present, so the insertion onto the calcaneus and the soleal line on the tibia can be demonstrated, but the triceps surae cannot be shown complete and the competency cannot be fully signed off here.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the attachments, actions and relations of the muscles of the deep posterior compartment of the leg and the course of the posterior tibial vessels.
structures: set of calcaneal branches of posterior tibial artery
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. All four deep compartment muscles and the main vessel are present, which is a complete muscular anchor. Note an asymmetry in the model: the fibular vein exists but the fibular artery does not, so the peroneal artery must be described against its vein. The tibial nerve is absent.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the four layers of the muscles of the sole of the foot with their attachments and actions.
structures: flexor digiti minimi brevis of foot
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Layers one, two and four anchor cleanly and the lumbricals are individually separated, which is good for teaching layer two. Layer three is incomplete: flexor hallucis brevis and adductor hallucis are absent. The dorsal interossei are also absent, so only the three plantar interossei can be shown and the PAD/DAB contrast cannot be taught on the model. The plantar aponeurosis and the medial and lateral plantar nerves are absent.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the formation, course and branches of the plantar arterial arch and the arterial supply of the sole.
structures: set of plantar digital arteries proper
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Strong anchor: the arch itself, its metatarsal and proper digital branches, and both parent vessels are all present, so the contribution of the deep plantar branch of dorsalis pedis to the arch is visible. The medial and lateral plantar arteries are not separately named in the model, so that step of the description has to be narrated.

competencies.statement: Explain the action of the long flexors, flexor accessorius and lumbricals on the toes and their role in the flexion of the digits.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed, and this one is more a functional item that departments often teach under the sole competency than a standalone AN code. Included because the model separates every lumbrical and every phalanx, so the oblique pull of flexor digitorum longus and its correction by flexor accessorius can actually be demonstrated in three dimensions rather than described.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the type, articular surfaces, movements, muscles producing the movements and blood supply of the hip joint.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Half the joint is missing: the hip bone and acetabulum are not in this region's structure list, nor are the iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments, the capsule, or the retinacular vessels. The competency is retained only because the muscles producing each movement, including the abductor mechanism and the lateral rotator group, are complete. Treat this as a muscle-action competency, not an articulation competency.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the type, articular surfaces, movements, muscles producing the movements and relations of the knee joint.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Bony articular surfaces and the muscles producing flexion, extension and unlocking are all present, and the role of popliteus in unlocking can be shown against the femur and tibia. Absent and therefore not demonstrable: the cruciate and collateral ligaments, both menisci, the capsule and the bursae, which is most of what the official knee competency examines.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the type, articular surfaces, movements and muscles producing the movements at the ankle joint.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. The mortise itself anchors well: tibia, fibula, interosseous membrane of leg and talus are all present, so the trochlear articulation and its wedge shape can be shown. The deltoid ligament, the lateral collateral complex and the inferior tibiofibular ligaments are absent, so ankle sprain applied anatomy cannot be taught on the model.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the movements of inversion and eversion, the joints at which they occur and the muscles producing them.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Well anchored: both axes of the transverse tarsal joint are visible as the talonavicular and calcaneocuboid articulations, and all four invertors and evertors present in the model are here. The spring ligament and the interosseous talocalcanean ligament are absent.

competencies.statement: Describe the medial and lateral longitudinal and the transverse arches of the foot, their bony and soft tissue factors of maintenance, and explain flat foot.
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Bony pillars of both longitudinal arches anchor completely, and the model contains the long plantar ligament plus the three main tie beam muscles, which is the core of the maintenance answer. Missing: the plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament, the short plantar ligament and the plantar aponeurosis, which are the other three factors students are expected to name.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the superficial and deep venous drainage of the lower limb, the perforating veins, and explain the anatomical basis of varicose veins.
competencies.topic: Venous drainage of the lower limb
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. Anchors completely, and the perforating veins existing as their own set is what makes the varicose vein reasoning teachable rather than verbal. Both saphenous terminations, at the femoral vein and the popliteal vein, are visible. The saphenofemoral junction tributaries and the deep fascia are not separately modelled.

competencies.statement: Describe and trace the continuity of the main arterial trunk of the lower limb from the femoral artery to the plantar arch, with its principal branches.
competencies.topic: Arterial supply of the lower limb
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed and the statement is a synthesis rather than a single official line, since most schemes split this across the thigh, leg and foot competencies. Flag the model's asymmetry: the profunda femoris artery and the medial circumflex femoral artery are absent while the deep femoral vein and medial circumflex femoral vein are present, so the trochanteric and cruciate anastomoses must be taught against the veins. The set of perforating arteries is present, which partly rescues the profunda story.

competencies.statement: Demonstrate the surface marking of the major arteries of the lower limb and the sites for palpating the femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses.
competencies.topic: Surface anatomy of the lower limb
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. All four pulse vessels exist, and the palpation landmarks that exist in the model are included: sartorius and adductor longus for the femoral pulse in the triangle, the calcaneal tendon for the posterior tibial pulse behind the medial malleolus, and the navicular tuberosity for the dorsalis pedis line. The inguinal ligament, the usual midinguinal point reference, is absent.

competencies.statement: Identify the bones of the lower limb and their ossification landmarks in an anteroposterior and lateral radiograph of the hip, knee, ankle and foot.
competencies.topic: Radiological anatomy of the lower limb
competencies.note: Code and wording reconstructed. The model supports the identification half of this competency well, since every bone a student must name on a lower limb film is present and separable, including the hallucal sesamoid that is commonly mistaken for a fracture. The radiographs themselves and the epiphyseal plates are of course not model content, so this is a naming and orientation exercise against 3D geometry, not radiograph reading.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts, articulations and features of the bony thoracic cage, including the sternum, typical ribs, costal cartilages and thoracic vertebrae, and their surface landmarks.
competencies.topic: Thoracic cage: osteology and surface landmarks
competencies.note: Reconstructed from memory, not quoted. I am reasonably confident the thorax block sits around AN18 to AN22 in the NMC CBME anatomy list, but the exact code number and sub-number are my reconstruction, and the wording is a paraphrase in NMC house style rather than a verbatim quotation. The sternal angle, jugular notch and costal margin are teaching points here but are not separately pinnable objects in this model.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the features of a typical rib and distinguish the atypical ribs, and explain the anatomical basis of rib fracture and of costal levels used in clinical examination.
structures: intervertebral disk of fifth thoracic vertebra
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The model carries every rib and every thoracic vertebra individually, so first, second, eleventh and twelfth rib can be contrasted against a typical rib on the same scene. Costovertebral and costotransverse joint capsules are not separate objects in this model.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the boundaries and contents of a typical intercostal space, the three layers of intercostal muscle, the neurovascular plane, and the anatomical basis of intercostal drain insertion.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Important honest caveat for the department: the intercostal NERVE is not in this model, so the vein-artery-nerve order in the costal groove can only be taught partially. The arterial and venous halves of the neurovascular bundle are present and pinnable.

competencies.statement: Describe the origin, course, relations and branches of the internal thoracic artery and its continuation as the superior epigastric artery, and explain its surgical importance in coronary artery bypass grafting.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The superior epigastric artery and vein are filed under abdomen in this model but are used here deliberately: the terminal bifurcation into musculophrenic and superior epigastric is the whole point of the competency and both branches exist.

competencies.statement: Describe the subdivisions of the mediastinum and enumerate and identify the contents of the superior and posterior mediastinum.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The transverse thoracic plane is definable here because both the manubrium and the fourth thoracic vertebra are separate objects. Vagus and phrenic nerves, thoracic duct and mediastinal lymph nodes are absent from the model, so the contents list a student can be shown is vascular, visceral and skeletal only.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the extent, relations and bifurcation of the trachea and the differences between the right and left principal bronchi, and explain the anatomical basis of foreign body inhalation into the right bronchus.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The model has no lungs, so this competency stops at the bronchi: bronchopulmonary segments, fissures and hilar arrangement cannot be demonstrated. Note also that the model lists both a main bronchus and a main bronchus proper, which is an ontology artefact rather than two anatomical entities, and staff should label them as one on the display.

competencies.statement: Describe the extent, course, curvatures, constrictions, relations and arterial supply of the oesophagus, and explain the anatomical basis of dysphagia and of oesophageal varices.
structures: set of oesophageal branches of thoracic aorta
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The model spells the organ esophagus but the aortic branches oesophageal, so both spellings appear in this structure list exactly as the model stores them. The left atrial relation is shown through wall of atrium, which is the only atrial object the model exposes.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the formation, course, tributaries and terminations of the azygos system of veins and explain its role as an alternative venous channel in caval obstruction.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The full caval-azygos-lumbar chain is intact in this model: ascending lumbar vein and inferior vena cava sit in the abdomen list and are included on purpose so the collateral route can be traced end to end on one screen.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the external features of the heart, the great vessels entering and leaving it, and the venous and arterial connections of each chamber.
competencies.topic: Heart: external features and great vessels
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Honest limit: this model exposes wall of atrium rather than named right and left atria and ventricles, so internal chamber features such as crista terminalis, fossa ovalis, trabeculae carneae and papillary muscles cannot be demonstrated. This competency should be marked partial in any coverage audit.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the coronary arterial supply and the venous drainage of the heart into the coronary sinus, and explain the anatomical basis of myocardial infarction and its regional distribution.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The venous side is well modelled: great, middle, small and posterior cardiac veins draining to the coronary sinus can all be pinned. The arterial side is weak: only trunk of coronary artery exists, with no named left anterior descending, circumflex or right coronary branches, so infarct territory teaching must be done on the venous pattern plus a diagram.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the位置, cusps and leaflets of the four cardiac valves, mark their anatomical position on the anterior chest wall, and relate each to its surface area of auscultation.
competencies.topic: Cardiac valves and areas of auscultation
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Correction the department should note: my statement above contains a stray non-English character in the word position, please read it as position. Coverage caveat: the mitral and tricuspid leaflets and two pulmonary cusps exist, but the aortic valve cusps and the left cusp of the pulmonary valve are not separate objects in this list, so the aortic area must be taught against ascending aorta and the sternal landmarks.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the origin, insertion, openings and vertebral levels of the diaphragm, name the structures traversing each opening, and explain the anatomical basis of diaphragmatic hernia.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. All three main openings can be demonstrated by their contents at T8, T10 and T12. The phrenic nerve is absent, so the motor supply half of this competency is diagram only. Psoas major, first lumbar vertebra and the phrenic vessels are drawn from the abdomen list to show the crura and arcuate ligament relations.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the layers, linea alba and arterial supply of the anterior abdominal wall, and explain the anatomical basis of surgical incisions and of the anastomosis between the superior and inferior epigastric arteries.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Serious coverage caveat: of the flat muscles only external oblique exists in this model, with no internal oblique, transversus abdominis, rectus abdominis or rectus sheath, and no inguinal canal or spermatic cord as objects. The deferent duct and testicular artery are included only so the cord contents can be pointed to indirectly. Treat the inguinal region competency as not demonstrable on this model.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the origin, course and branches of the coeliac trunk and trace the arterial supply of the foregut derivatives.
competencies.topic: Coeliac trunk and foregut arterial supply
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The model duplicates the same vessel under several ontology names, celiac artery and celiac trunk, and hepatic artery proper and trunk of hepatic artery, which is useful for search but should be labelled as one vessel in teaching. Left and right gastric and the gastroduodenal artery are not separately named, only a generic gastric artery.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts, relations, blood supply and lymphatic drainage of the stomach and explain the anatomical basis of referred pain and of gastric ulcer perforation.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The stomach is a single object here, so parts such as fundus, body, pyloric antrum and the greater and lesser curvatures cannot be pinned individually. Relations to the pancreas, spleen and lesser sac bed can be shown by isolating neighbours. Gastric lymph nodes are absent, so the lymphatic half of the competency is diagram only.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts, relations and blood supply of the duodenum and the pancreas, and the arrangement of the pancreatic duct system, and explain the anatomical basis of obstructive jaundice in carcinoma of the head of the pancreas.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Strong coverage here: the pancreatic duct tree is modelled separately from the parenchyma, so the duct system can be shown inside a transparent gland. The four parts of the duodenum are not separate objects. The superior mesenteric vessels crossing the third part are present, so superior mesenteric artery syndrome can be demonstrated positionally.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the lobes, surfaces, peritoneal relations and segmental arterial supply of the liver, the components of the portal triad and the drainage of the hepatic veins into the inferior vena cava.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. This is the best supported abdominal competency in the model: eight segmental hepatic arteries are individually named, so Couinaud segmentation can be taught properly, which most plastic models cannot do. I have listed four of the eight to stay within the structure cap, the remaining segmental arteries are anterior inferior, posterior superior, medial inferior and lateral superior. Caudate lobe is the only named lobe.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts of the extrahepatic biliary apparatus, the formation of the bile duct, and explain the anatomical basis of gall stone impaction and of Calot triangle in cholecystectomy.
structures: duct of caudate lobe of liver
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Note for the department: the model exposes cystic duct, hepatic duct and common hepatic duct, but there is no separate object named bile duct or common bile duct, and no hepatopancreatic ampulla or sphincter, so the terminal part of the biliary tree and its union with the pancreatic duct must be taught on a diagram. Calot triangle can be approximated from cystic duct, common hepatic duct and hepatic artery proper.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the formation, course and tributaries of the portal vein, enumerate the sites of portosystemic anastomosis, and explain the anatomical basis of oesophageal varices, caput medusae and haemorrhoids.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Four ontology aliases for the portal vein appear in the model, hepatic portal vein, portal vein, trunk of portal vein and pre-hepatic portal vein, and staff should present them as one vessel. All three classic anastomotic sites can be pointed to by their organ, oesophagus, rectum and the periumbilical veins through inferior epigastric vein, even though the anastomosing tributaries themselves are not modelled.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the extent, mesentery, and superior mesenteric arterial and venous supply of the small intestine, and explain the anatomical basis of midgut volvulus and of intestinal ischaemia.
competencies.topic: Small intestine, mesentery and superior mesenteric vessels
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Real gap: there are no jejunum and ileum objects in this list, only the mesentery and the ileocaecal junction, so the jejunum versus ileum comparison, arcades and vasa recta cannot be demonstrated. The root of the mesentery running from the duodenojejunal flexure to the ileocaecal junction can be traced.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts and distinguishing features of the large intestine, the positions of the vermiform appendix and its mesoappendix, and the territory of the inferior mesenteric artery, and explain the anatomical basis of appendicitis pain and of the ileocaecal junction.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. In the official scheme the caecum and appendix and the colon are usually two separate competencies, I have merged them here because the structure sets overlap heavily. Strong point: all three taeniae coli are individually named, so the convergence of taeniae onto the base of the appendix, the standard operative landmark, can be demonstrated. Caecum and sigmoid colon are not separate objects.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the position, surfaces, relations, peritoneal attachments and blood supply of the spleen, and explain the anatomical basis of splenic rupture and of the surface marking along the ninth to eleventh ribs.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Ribs nine to eleven come from the thorax list and are included deliberately, the surface marking of the spleen along the long axis of the tenth rib is the examinable point and both the organ and the ribs are pinnable together. The lienorenal and gastrosplenic ligaments are not modelled.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the position, coverings, relations, hilar structures and blood supply of the kidney, the course and constrictions of the ureter, and the suprarenal gland, and explain the anatomical basis of renal colic and of the loin approach to the kidney.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Coverage is good: the twelfth rib relation, the psoas bed, the aortic and caval connections and the left testicular vein draining into the left renal vein are all demonstrable, which covers the classic left varicocele question. Internal renal architecture, calyces, pelvis, pyramids and cortex, is not exposed as separate objects.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the muscles of the posterior abdominal wall and the course, relations and segmental branches of the abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava on the lumbar vertebral column.
competencies.topic: Posterior abdominal wall, abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava
structures: intervertebral disk of fourth lumbar vertebra
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Quadratus lumborum is absent from the list, so the posterior wall muscle set is incomplete. The lumbar plexus is absent entirely, so the nerve half of this competency, including femoral, obturator and genitofemoral nerves emerging from psoas, is diagram only. All five lumbar vertebrae and their discs exist, so the L4 bifurcation level can be shown accurately.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the bony pelvis, the muscles forming the pelvic diaphragm and their attachment to the tendinous arch, and explain the role of levator ani in pelvic support and continence and the anatomical basis of the anorectal angle.
competencies.topic: Bony pelvis, pelvic diaphragm and anal sphincter
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. In the official scheme the bony pelvis, the pelvic diaphragm and the anal canal are separate competencies, I merged them because the model has no anal canal object and no coccyx, so an anal canal competency alone would fall below the two structure threshold. The three named parts of levator ani plus coccygeus and the tendinous arch are all present, which is unusually complete, and the puborectalis sling around the anorectal junction can be demonstrated directly.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the origin, course and branches of the internal iliac artery and the venous drainage of the pelvis, and explain the anatomical basis of internal iliac ligation and of the pelvic venous plexuses.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. Asymmetry the department should know about: the venous tributaries of the internal iliac vein are richly modelled, obturator, superior and inferior gluteal, internal pudendal, lateral sacral and median sacral, but the matching named arteries are not, only the internal iliac trunk. Teach branch patterns on the venous side and mirror them onto the artery.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the position, parts, relations, interior and supports of the urinary bladder and the parts of the male urethra, and explain the anatomical basis of suprapubic cystostomy and of urethral catheterisation and rupture.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The urethra is one continuous object, so the prostatic, membranous, bulbar and penile parts cannot be pinned separately, but their extents can be shown by isolating the prostate and the corpus spongiosum around it. The trigone, ureteric orifices and internal urethral sphincter are not separate objects, so bladder interior teaching stays on diagrams.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the position, lobes, capsule, relations and duct openings of the prostate, and explain the anatomical basis of benign prostatic hyperplasia, of digital rectal examination and of the spread of prostatic carcinoma.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The prostate is a single object, so the median, lateral and posterior lobes and the zonal anatomy used clinically cannot be pinned. The relation to the rectum posteriorly, the bladder neck above, and the seminal vesicle and deferent duct forming the ejaculatory duct are all demonstrable. The prostatic venous plexus is not modelled, so vertebral venous spread must be taught from a diagram.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the testis, epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle, their arterial supply and venous drainage, and explain the anatomical basis of varicocele and of the lymphatic spread of testicular tumours to para-aortic nodes.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. In the NMC scheme testicular descent and the coverings of the testis sit in the abdomen chapter while the ducts sit in the pelvis chapter, I have filed this under pelvis because that is where the model stores the organs. The testicular vessels are drawn from the abdomen list, deliberately, since the left testicular vein to left renal vein and right to inferior vena cava asymmetry is the examinable point. Tunica vaginalis, gubernaculum and pampiniform plexus are absent.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts and erectile tissues of the penis, its arterial supply and venous drainage, and explain the anatomical basis of erection and of the relation of the urethra to the corpus spongiosum.
competencies.note: Code reconstructed from memory, wording paraphrased. The three erectile bodies, the glans and both the dorsal artery and the superficial dorsal vein are present, so this competency is well anchored. The deep dorsal vein, deep artery of the penis, bulbospongiosus and ischiocavernosus, and the perineal membrane are absent. Skin and pubic hair are generic surface objects in the model rather than region specific, use them only for orientation. Separately, the pelvis list also contains distal phalanx of thumb and proximal phalanx of thumb, which are clearly mis-filed upper limb objects and should be excluded from any pelvis assessment set.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the features of a typical cervical vertebra, the atlas, the axis and the seventh cervical vertebra, and the intervertebral discs of the cervical column.
competencies.topic: Osteology of the cervical vertebral column
structures: intervertebral disk of third cervical vertebra
intervertebral disk of fourth cervical vertebra
intervertebral disk of sixth cervical vertebra
intervertebral disk of seventh cervical vertebra
competencies.note: Code number and sub-numbering RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the NMC CBME 2019 Anatomy competency document; I am not quoting a copy of it. I recall cervical osteology sitting early in the AN29 head-and-neck block but cannot vouch for the decimal. Statement is written in CBME house style, paraphrased, not verbatim. Structure names are QUOTED EXACTLY from the supplied list. Model gives no vertebral foramen/transverse foramen sub-parts, so foramen transversarium content must be taught on the whole-bone mesh.

competencies.statement: Identify the individual bones of the cranium and face in norma frontalis, norma lateralis, norma verticalis and norma basalis, and demonstrate the sutures and bony landmarks between them.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory, not quoted. Statement paraphrased in CBME style. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Note for the department: the model supplies whole bones only, so named foramina, fossae and sutures are not separately pinnable; palatine bone and inferior nasal concha exist and can be added if the scheme wants them here rather than under the nose competency. Temporal bone is a single mesh, so petrous/squamous/tympanic parts cannot be tagged.

competencies.statement: Describe the boundaries of the bony orbit, name the bones that form its roof, floor, medial and lateral walls, and identify the common tendinous ring at its apex.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted; orbit content in the NMC scheme may be numbered under the orbit topic rather than the scalp/face topic and departments should re-anchor it. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Superior and inferior orbital fissures and the optic canal are not separate meshes, so aperture teaching must be done on the assembled bones.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the skeletal and cartilaginous framework of the external nose and the nasal septum, and the bones forming the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory; I associate the nose with the AN39 range but cannot confirm the decimal. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Caution: 'lateral nasal cartilage' is tagged in the neuro batch of the source file, not the head-neck batch, but the mesh exists and pins correctly. Superior and middle conchae (part of the ethmoid mesh) and the paranasal sinuses are NOT separately present, so sinus competencies cannot be anchored here.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles, their attachments to the hyoid bone and their role in the subdivisions of the anterior triangle of the neck.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the AN34 anterior-triangle topic; decimal not reliable. Statement paraphrased in CBME style. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Strong anchor: the model carries the full suprahyoid and infrahyoid set including the digastric intermediate tendon. Nerve supply (ansa cervicalis, mylohyoid nerve) cannot be demonstrated: no cervical plexus or facial nerve branches in this model.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the carotid system in the neck, the contents of the carotid sheath and the great vessels at the root of the neck.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Honest gap: the external carotid artery and its named branches, the vagus nerve, the thyroid gland itself and the thyrocervical trunk are absent from this list, so the classic 'branches of external carotid' and 'blood supply of thyroid' competencies cannot be anchored and were deliberately skipped. Scalenus anterior is included as the surgical landmark for the subclavian relations.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the prevertebral and scalene muscles, their attachments to the cervical vertebrae, and the course of the vertebral artery through the deep structures of the neck.
structures: superior oblique part of longus colli
vertical intermediate part of longus colli
inferior oblique part of longus colli
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the AN37 deep-neck topic; decimal uncertain. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, including the three named parts of longus colli, which is an unusually good anchor: most atlases show it as one muscle and the model separates it. Cervical sympathetic chain and phrenic nerve are absent, so the sympathetic-trunk half of this competency has no geometry.

competencies.statement: Describe the boundaries and contents of the suboccipital triangle and demonstrate the four suboccipital muscles and their attachments to the atlas, axis and occipital bone.
competencies.topic: Suboccipital region and back of the neck
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted; the back-of-neck topic number is one I am least sure of in this block. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Complete anchor for the triangle: all four suboccipital muscles, the third part of the vertebral artery, and the roofing muscles are present. The suboccipital nerve and greater occipital nerve are absent, so contents teaching is vascular only.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the submandibular region: the submandibular and sublingual salivary glands, their relations, and the muscles forming the floor of the mouth.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the AN36 submandibular topic. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Honest gap: the submandibular duct, lingual nerve, hypoglossal nerve and submandibular ganglion are absent, so the classic duct-and-nerve crossing relation cannot be shown. The glands and all four floor muscles are present, which is enough for relations and bed teaching.

competencies.statement: Describe the parts and extrinsic muscles of the tongue and demonstrate their attachments to the mandible and hyoid bone.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Deliberately narrowed: styloglossus and palatoglossus are NOT in the model, so only two of the four extrinsic muscles can be shown and the competency wording has been trimmed to match. Intrinsic muscles, lingual papillae, the lingual artery and the nerve supply have no geometry, so the standard 'blood supply and nerve supply of tongue' competency was skipped rather than half-anchored.

competencies.statement: Identify the permanent teeth of the maxillary and mandibular arches by class and position, and demonstrate the gingiva of the upper and lower jaws.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted; in the medical CBME scheme dentition sits inside the oral cavity topic, while BDS schemes carry a far more detailed dental set, so dental faculty should re-code this entirely. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, including the model's 'secondary' wording for permanent teeth, which is Terminologia usage, not the FDI or Indian textbook usage students will hear in class. Third molars are absent from the list. Twelve-structure cap forced a representative selection; the remaining premolars and molars are also present.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the muscles of the soft palate and the pharyngeal constrictor and longitudinal muscles, their attachments and the raphes that anchor them.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory; the palate and pharynx may be split across two AN codes in the official scheme and this maps them as one demonstrable set. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Very strong anchor: all three constrictors, all three longitudinal muscles, four palatal muscles and both raphes are present. Missing: palatoglossus, the pharyngeal plexus, Killian's dehiscence and the palatine tonsil, so nerve supply and the piriform fossa cannot be demonstrated.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the cartilages, membranes and ligaments of the larynx and demonstrate the boundaries of the laryngeal inlet and the cricothyroid membrane.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the AN40 larynx topic; decimal uncertain. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Excellent anchor: all five cartilages plus six named membranes and ligaments. Note the epiglottic cartilage itself is not on the list even though two of its ligaments are, so the inlet must be taught around an absent epiglottis. Clinically relevant: the median cricothyroid ligament is present, which supports cricothyrotomy teaching.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the intrinsic muscles of the larynx and explain their actions on the vocal ligament in abduction, adduction, tension and relaxation of the vocal folds.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. The complete intrinsic set is present, including vocalis as a separate mesh from thyro-arytenoid and both parts of cricothyroid, which lets the oblique-versus-straight action be shown properly. The recurrent laryngeal and external laryngeal nerves are absent, so the standard 'nerve supply and effects of nerve injury' half of the larynx competency cannot be anchored and has been left out of the wording.

competencies.statement: Describe and demonstrate the extraocular muscles, their origin from the common tendinous ring, their insertions and their actions on the eyeball.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the AN33 orbit topic; decimal uncertain. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. The single best-served competency in this block: all six extraocular muscles, levator palpebrae superioris with a separate tendon mesh, the common tendinous ring, the trochlea and both check ligaments. Suitable for action testing and for the H-test clinical correlation.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve and its branches, the trochlear nerve, and the superior and inferior divisions of the oculomotor nerve within the orbit.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Important scope note for the department: the orbit is the ONLY place in this model where named peripheral nerves exist. There is no facial nerve, no trigeminal ganglion, no maxillary or mandibular division, no cervical plexus and no brachial plexus, so every other cranial-nerve competency in the head-and-neck block was skipped as unanchorable. The abducent nerve is also absent despite lateral rectus being present.

competencies.statement: Describe the location, roots and branches of the ciliary ganglion and trace the parasympathetic pathway to the intra-ocular muscles.
structures: communicating branch of nasociliary nerve with ciliary ganglion
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, including the long form 'communicating branch of nasociliary nerve with ciliary ganglion', which is the sensory root. Motor root (from the inferior branch of oculomotor) and sensory root are both present; the sympathetic root is not, so the pathway can be taught two thirds of the way. Sphincter and dilator pupillae are absent, so the effector end is shown on the iris mesh only.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the three coats of the eyeball and the refractive media, and demonstrate the contents of the anterior chamber and the attachment of the lens.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory of the AN42 eyeball topic; decimal uncertain. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Note the model names the retina 'optic part of retina' and the ciliary processes 'corona ciliaris', both Terminologia forms that differ from Indian textbook wording, so labels should be glossed for students. The posterior chamber, central artery of the retina and the ciliary body as a whole are absent, so aqueous circulation and glaucoma correlation are only partly demonstrable.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the eyelids and the lacrimal apparatus, and trace the flow of tears from the lacrimal gland to the inferior meatus of the nose.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Unusually complete: the whole tear pathway from gland through lake, canaliculus, sac and duct is present, and the inferior nasal concha lets the drainage endpoint be shown. Orbicularis oculi, the conjunctiva and the tarsal glands are absent, so lid closure and the palpebral fissure cannot be demonstrated.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts of the ventricular system, the connections between them, and trace the formation and circulation of cerebrospinal fluid.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED from memory; I recall the neuroanatomy block sitting in the AN55 to AN72 range but the topic-to-number mapping here is a reconstruction and departments must re-code against their own scheme. Statement paraphrased in CBME style. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. The full ventricular chain is present. Missing: the foramina of Luschka and Magendie, the subarachnoid cisterns and the arachnoid granulations, so CSF absorption cannot be shown, only production and internal flow. Caution when browsing the raw list: 'cavity of ventricle' and 'wall of ventricle' in the neuro batch are cardiac, not cerebral, and must not be used here.

competencies.statement: Identify the gyri and lobes on the superolateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere and localise the primary motor, primary somatosensory and receptive language areas on them.
structures: anterior part of superior temporal gyrus
posterior part of superior temporal gyrus
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. The superior temporal gyrus is split into anterior and posterior parts in this model, which is convenient for localising Wernicke's area. Functional-area teaching must be done by pointing at gyri: there are no Brodmann-area meshes, no central or lateral sulcus meshes (only the arteries named after them), and no inferior parietal lobule as a single object.

competencies.statement: Identify the gyri and structures on the medial and inferior surfaces of the cerebral hemisphere, including the corpus callosum, cingulate gyrus and the insula deep to the lateral sulcus.
competencies.topic: Cerebral hemisphere: medial and inferior surfaces
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Honest gaps that change what can be examined: there is no calcarine sulcus, no cuneus, no precuneus, no paracentral lobule and no uncus in this model, so the standard medial-surface visual-cortex landmark teaching has to be done on 'occipital lobe' as a whole. Corpus callosum is one mesh, so genu, body, splenium and rostrum cannot be separately pinned.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the arteries forming the circle of Willis and the major cerebral arteries, and correlate their territories with the clinical features of occlusion.
structures: sphenoid part of middle cerebral artery
insular part of middle cerebral artery
precommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
postcommunicating part of posterior cerebral artery
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, and note the model uses segmental Terminologia naming (sphenoid and insular parts for M1 and M2, precommunicating and postcommunicating for P1 and P2) rather than the M1/M2/P1/P2 shorthand students will meet in radiology. Honest gap: the anterior and posterior communicating arteries are NOT in this list, so the circle of Willis cannot actually be closed on screen. Teach it as the major feeding vessels plus their branches, and say so to students. Internal carotid and vertebral arteries are drawn from the head-neck batch.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the components of the basal ganglia and the parts and relations of the internal capsule, and correlate the capsular territory with the clinical picture of a capsular stroke.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Caudate, putamen and globus pallidus are separate meshes, so lentiform and striatum can be built up in front of the student. Internal capsule is a single mesh: anterior limb, genu and posterior limb cannot be pinned individually, so somatotopy of the corticospinal fibres must be described, not demonstrated. Claustrum, subthalamic nucleus and substantia nigra are absent, so the extrapyramidal circuit competency was not attempted.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the parts of the diencephalon, the boundaries and recesses of the third ventricle, and the epithalamic and subthalamic structures related to it.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Strong anchor: both geniculate bodies, the full epithalamus (pineal body, habenula, stria medullaris of thalamus) and the hypothalamic surface landmarks are present. Thalamic nuclei are not subdivided, so nuclear-group teaching stays diagrammatic. Subthalamic nucleus absent.

competencies.statement: Describe the location, parts and relations of the hypophysis cerebri and its connection to the hypothalamus, and correlate an expanding pituitary lesion with visual field loss.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted; the pituitary may sit under the cranial-cavity topic in the head-and-neck block rather than under neuroanatomy in the official scheme, and the region assignment here is my editorial choice. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, drawing pituitary gland and sphenoid bone from the head-neck batch and the rest from the neuro batch. Pituitary gland is one mesh: adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis are not separable, and there is no infundibulum, no sella turcica sub-mesh and no cavernous sinus. The chiasm-plus-pituitary pair is still enough for the bitemporal hemianopia correlation.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the external features of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata, and demonstrate the colliculi, their brachia and the interpeduncular fossa.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased and deliberately restricted to EXTERNAL features. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. The internal-structure competencies of the brainstem (cranial nerve nuclei, medial lemniscus, olive, pyramid, cerebral peduncle crus versus tegmentum, transverse sections at named levels) cannot be anchored: this model has no brainstem nuclei, no tracts and no attached cranial nerve roots. Both colliculi with both brachia are present, which supports auditory and visual reflex pathway teaching.

competencies.statement: Describe the position and relations of the cerebellum in the posterior cranial fossa, its relationship to the fourth ventricle and the tentorium cerebelli, and its blood supply.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased and deliberately narrowed to relations and blood supply. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY. Be honest with students here: cerebellum is a SINGLE mesh in this model. There are no hemispheres, no vermis, no flocculonodular lobe, no tonsil and no superior, middle or inferior cerebellar peduncles, so lobar subdivision, functional zones and tonsillar herniation cannot be demonstrated. Only PICA is present of the three cerebellar arteries. Departments that need cerebellar internal anatomy should not use this model for it.

competencies.statement: Describe and identify the components of the limbic system and trace the Papez circuit from the hippocampus through the fornix and mammillary body to the thalamus and cingulate gyrus.
