competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, including 'fornix of forebrain' and 'commissure of fornix of forebrain', which are the model's forms for the fornix and its commissure. Genuinely strong anchor: the entire Papez circuit can be traced on geometry except the mammillothalamic tract, which is absent. Dentate gyrus, subiculum and olfactory structures are also absent, so hippocampal internal circuitry and the olfactory pathway competency were skipped.

competencies.statement: Trace the visual pathway from the retina to the visual cortex and correlate lesions at each point with the resulting visual field defect.
competencies.note: Code RECONSTRUCTED, not quoted; the visual pathway may be numbered with the special senses rather than in the neuroanatomy sequence in the official scheme. Statement paraphrased. Structure names QUOTED EXACTLY, drawing 'optic part of retina' and 'optic nerve' from the head-neck batch. The pathway is intact from retina to lateral geniculate body, and the superior colliculus limb supports the pupillary light reflex. Beyond the geniculate body there is no optic radiation and no calcarine or primary visual cortex mesh, so the last leg must be taught on 'occipital lobe' and the white matter of the hemisphere as a proxy. Meyer's loop and the two-and-a-half-neuron light reflex arc cannot be demonstrated.

topics.topic: Male versus female bony pelvis: general build
topics.male_form: Heavier, thicker bones with rough, well marked muscle impressions. Ilium tall and set more vertically, iliac fossa deep. Whole pelvis is deep and narrow, built for weight transmission and locomotion in a heavier frame. Greater pelvis shallow relative to height of the ilium.
topics.female_form: Lighter, thinner, smoother bones with faint muscle markings. Ilium is lower and flared laterally, iliac fossa shallow, so the iliac crests lie further apart while the acetabula stay comparatively close. Whole pelvis is broad and shallow, built as a birth canal. Greater pelvis wide, giving the characteristic wider hip contour.
topics.why_examined: Question one of every general anatomy viva on the pelvis, and the anchor question in the pelvis chapter of BD Chaurasia and Cunningham's. Also the standard first year osteology spot.
topics.clinical: Anthropological and forensic sex determination of skeletal remains. Also underlies the wider female hip contour that governs gait mechanics and hip loading.
topics.exam_q: Q. Give four general differences between the male and the female pelvis as a whole. A. Female bones lighter and smoother with faint markings, ilium more flared and less vertical, pelvis broad and shallow rather than deep and narrow, greater pelvis wider with more widely separated iliac crests.

topics.topic: Pelvic inlet: heart shaped versus transversely oval
anchor_structures: intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra
topics.male_form: Inlet is heart shaped or cardiform because the sacral promontory projects forward strongly and indents the brim. Anteroposterior and transverse diameters are more nearly equal. Pelvic brim is rounded and blunt.
topics.female_form: Inlet is transversely oval or nearly circular, because the promontory is less prominent and the ilia are flared. Standard obstetric diameters: true or anatomical conjugate about 11 cm, transverse about 13 cm, oblique about 12 cm. The transverse diameter clearly exceeds the anteroposterior diameter.
topics.why_examined: Standard MBBS long answer, and the entry point for the obstetric pelvis in second year and in obstetrics. Numbers are asked directly.
topics.clinical: A contracted inlet with true conjugate under 10 cm predicts cephalopelvic disproportion and failure of the head to engage. Diagonal conjugate is measured clinically from the lower border of the pubic symphysis to the promontory, about 12.5 cm, and the obstetric conjugate is estimated by subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm.
topics.exam_q: Q. Name the diameters of the female pelvic inlet with their values, and state the shape of the inlet in each sex. A. Anteroposterior or true conjugate 11 cm, oblique 12 cm, transverse 13 cm. Male inlet is heart shaped, female inlet is transversely oval.

topics.topic: Subpubic angle and the pubic arch
topics.male_form: Subpubic angle is narrow, roughly 50 to 60 degrees, shaped like an inverted V. The ischiopubic rami are everted where the crura of the penis attach, and the arch is deep and narrow.
topics.female_form: Subpubic angle is wide, roughly 80 to 90 degrees, shaped like a rounded U. The rami are less everted and the arch is shallow and rounded, so the fetal head can occupy it as it extends under the symphysis.
topics.why_examined: The single most quoted difference in every Indian and Gulf MBBS paper, and the most reliable single visual trait in forensic sexing of the pelvis.
topics.clinical: A narrow subpubic arch reduces the effective outlet and forces the head posteriorly onto the perineum, increasing perineal tearing and the need for episiotomy. Assessed on clinical pelvimetry by admitting two fingers under the arch in the male pattern versus a fist across the intertuberous diameter in the female pattern.
topics.exam_q: Q. State the subpubic angle in each sex and its obstetric significance. A. Male about 50 to 60 degrees and V shaped, female about 80 to 90 degrees and U shaped. The wide female arch accommodates the fetal head during extension at the outlet.

topics.topic: Greater sciatic notch and ischial spines
topics.male_form: Greater sciatic notch is narrow and deep, subtending roughly 50 to 60 degrees, and admits about two fingers. Ischial spines are prominent and inverted, projecting into the pelvic cavity, so the interspinous diameter is reduced.
topics.female_form: Greater sciatic notch is wide and shallow, approaching a right angle, and admits about three fingers. Ischial spines are less prominent and everted, giving an interspinous diameter of about 10.5 cm, which is the narrowest plane of the whole female pelvis.
topics.why_examined: Asked as a paired difference in the pelvis long answer, and used in forensic anthropology because the notch survives fragmentation.
topics.clinical: The ischial spine is the landmark for transvaginal pudendal nerve block, the reference point for assessing fetal station in labour, station zero being at the spines, and the attachment of the sacrospinous ligament used in sacrospinous colpopexy for vault prolapse.
topics.exam_q: Q. How does the greater sciatic notch differ in the two sexes, and what is the clinical importance of the ischial spine? A. Narrow, about 50 to 60 degrees in the male, wide and near a right angle in the female. The spine gives fetal station zero, is the landmark for pudendal block, and anchors the sacrospinous ligament.

topics.topic: Sacrum: shape, promontory and auricular surface
topics.male_form: Sacrum is long, narrow and evenly curved through its length. The promontory is prominent and projects forward into the inlet. The auricular surface extends over about two and a half to three vertebrae. Sacral index, that is breadth over length times 100, is lower, of the order of 105.
topics.female_form: Sacrum is short, wide and set more vertically, the upper part relatively flat with the sharper curve confined to the lower part, which enlarges the cavity. The promontory is less prominent. The auricular surface extends over about two to two and a half vertebrae. Sacral index is higher, of the order of 115.
topics.why_examined: Part of the classic tabulated comparison, and separately examinable in vertebral column osteology and in forensic medicine.
topics.clinical: The promontory is the posterior landmark for the obstetric conjugate and is palpated on diagonal conjugate measurement. It is also the entry landmark for laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy, where the left common iliac vein lies dangerously close in the midline.
topics.exam_q: Q. Compare the male and female sacrum. A. Male: long, narrow, uniformly curved, prominent promontory, auricular surface over three vertebrae. Female: short, broad, upper part flat with lower curve, less prominent promontory, auricular surface over two to two and a half vertebrae.

topics.topic: Obturator foramen, acetabulum and the ischiopubic ramus
topics.male_form: Obturator foramen is large and oval. Acetabulum is large, about 50 to 52 mm in diameter, and faces laterally. Its diameter is greater than the distance from the anterior acetabular margin to the pubic symphysis. Body of the pubis is triangular and the ischiopubic ramus is everted with a rough crural attachment area.
topics.female_form: Obturator foramen is small and triangular. Acetabulum is smaller, about 44 to 46 mm, and faces more anterolaterally, which contributes to the greater bicondylar angle at the knee. Acetabular diameter approximately equals the distance from its anterior margin to the symphysis. Body of the pubis is square or rectangular, and the ischiopubic ramus is narrow with a sharp inferior edge, one of the Phenice traits.
topics.why_examined: Tabulated in the standard pelvis comparison and specifically asked in forensic medicine as part of pubic sexing.
topics.clinical: Phenice traits of the pubis, that is the ventral arc, the subpubic concavity and the sharp medial ischiopubic ramus, give roughly 95 percent accuracy in sex determination from a single bone. Acetabular orientation is relevant to hip dysplasia and to component positioning in arthroplasty.
topics.exam_q: Q. Name the three Phenice traits and state their value. A. Ventral arc, subpubic concavity, and the sharp medial aspect of the ischiopubic ramus, all present in the female pubis, giving about 95 percent accuracy in sex determination.

topics.topic: Pelvic cavity and outlet, obstetric diameters
topics.male_form: Cavity is long, funnel shaped and narrows towards the outlet, because the side walls converge and the ischial tuberosities are inverted. The outlet is small and the intertuberous distance is narrow. Depth from the promontory to the tip of the coccyx is greater.
topics.female_form: Cavity is short, roughly cylindrical, with parallel side walls, so the head can descend without progressive narrowing. Outlet: anteroposterior diameter about 12.5 to 13 cm, transverse or intertuberous about 10.5 to 11 cm. The anteroposterior outlet diameter increases by 2 to 3 cm during labour as the coccyx is pushed back.
topics.why_examined: The core obstetric anatomy question, asked in anatomy and again in obstetrics. Numbers are examined directly.
topics.clinical: Outlet contraction with an intertuberous diameter under 8 cm predicts obstructed labour and deep transverse arrest. The mobile sacrococcygeal joint is why coccygeal fracture or fusion matters in labour, and why the squatting position enlarges the outlet.
topics.exam_q: Q. Give the diameters of the female pelvic outlet and explain why the anteroposterior diameter increases in labour. A. Anteroposterior about 12.5 to 13 cm, transverse or intertuberous about 10.5 to 11 cm. The coccyx is retropulsed at the mobile sacrococcygeal joint, adding 2 to 3 cm.

topics.topic: Caldwell and Moloy pelvic types
topics.male_form: The android pattern is the typical male form: heart shaped inlet, convergent side walls, prominent inverted ischial spines, narrow forepelvis, narrow subpubic arch, and a straight forward sloping sacrum.
topics.female_form: Four types are recognised. Gynaecoid, the classic female pelvis, in about 50 percent of women, rounded inlet and roomy at all levels. Anthropoid, oval with the long axis anteroposterior, about 25 percent. Android, about 20 percent, male pattern in a woman and the type most associated with obstructed labour. Platypelloid or flat, under 5 percent, with a wide transverse and short anteroposterior inlet.
topics.why_examined: Standard obstetrics viva and increasingly asked in anatomy as applied anatomy of the pelvis.
topics.clinical: Android pelvis favours deep transverse arrest and persistent occipitoposterior position. Anthropoid favours direct occipitoposterior delivery. Platypelloid causes arrest at the inlet. Type prediction is now clinical and by trial of labour, since routine radiographic pelvimetry has been abandoned.
topics.exam_q: Q. Classify the pelvis according to Caldwell and Moloy and name the type most likely to cause obstructed labour. A. Gynaecoid, android, anthropoid and platypelloid. The android pelvis, essentially a male shaped pelvis in a woman, is the type most associated with obstructed labour.

topics.topic: Levator ani: levator prostatae versus pubovaginalis, and the urogenital hiatus
topics.male_form: The most medial fibres of pubococcygeus sweep round the prostate and are named levator prostatae, supporting the gland and blending with the sphincter urethrae. The hiatus in the pelvic floor transmits only the urethra and the anal canal, so the floor is comparatively intact and strong.
topics.female_form: The corresponding medial fibres pass beside the vagina as pubovaginalis, which acts as a sphincter for the vagina and supports the bladder neck. The urogenital hiatus is wider because it must transmit the urethra, the vagina and the anal canal, which is the anatomical basis of the female predisposition to pelvic organ prolapse.
topics.why_examined: Named parts of levator ani are a guaranteed viva item, and the sex specific part is the discriminating question that separates a good answer from an average one.
topics.clinical: Avulsion of pubococcygeus from the pubic bone during vaginal delivery, seen in about 15 to 20 percent of first vaginal births on ultrasound, predisposes to cystocele, uterine prolapse and stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises target exactly these fibres.
topics.exam_q: Q. Name the parts of levator ani and state which part differs between the sexes. A. Pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus and puborectalis, with coccygeus completing the pelvic diaphragm. The medial pubococcygeal fibres form levator prostatae in the male and pubovaginalis in the female.

topics.topic: Perineal body and obstetric anal sphincter injury
topics.male_form: The perineal body lies between the bulb of the penis and the anal canal. It is small, less than 1 cm, and functionally unimportant because it is never subjected to stretching. Rupture is essentially confined to trauma.
topics.female_form: A pyramidal fibromuscular node about 1.25 cm, lying between the vaginal vestibule and the anal canal, into which bulbospongiosus, the superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles, the external anal sphincter and levator ani all converge. It is the keystone of the female perineum and the structure divided or torn in childbirth.
topics.why_examined: Classic short note across anatomy, obstetrics and surgery. Examiners ask which muscles converge on it.
topics.clinical: Episiotomy, preferably mediolateral to avoid extension into the anal sphincter, is an incision through this body. Obstetric anal sphincter injury is graded 3a with under 50 percent of the external sphincter torn, 3b over 50 percent, 3c internal sphincter involved, and 4 with anal mucosa breached. Unrepaired injury causes faecal incontinence and later prolapse.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is the perineal body and which muscles are attached to it? A. A fibromuscular node in the centre of the perineum, prominent in the female between the vagina and the anal canal, receiving bulbospongiosus, the superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles, the external anal sphincter and levator ani.

topics.topic: Urethra: length, parts and curvatures
topics.male_form: About 18 to 20 cm long, in four parts: preprostatic about 1 cm, prostatic 3 to 4 cm and the widest and most dilatable part, membranous 1 to 2 cm which is the narrowest part apart from the external meatus and the least dilatable, and spongy about 15 cm. It has two curves, one fixed at the bulb and one prepubic curve that is abolished when the penis is elevated for catheterisation.
topics.female_form: About 4 cm long and 6 mm wide, running downwards and forwards from the internal urethral orifice, firmly embedded in the anterior wall of the vagina, opening in the vestibule about 2.5 cm behind the glans clitoris. It corresponds developmentally only to the part of the male urethra above the openings of the ejaculatory ducts. It is straight, dilatable and has no prostatic part.
topics.why_examined: Male urethra is a certain long answer or short note. The comparison is the standard follow up question, and the clinical link to catheterisation is asked in every clinical viva.
topics.clinical: The short straight female urethra and its proximity to the vaginal introitus and anus explain the far higher incidence of urinary tract infection in women. In the male, catheter resistance is met at the membranous urethra, and false passage or urethral rupture is a real hazard. Straddle injury ruptures the bulbar urethra in the male, an injury with no common female counterpart.
topics.exam_q: Q. Name the parts of the male urethra with their lengths and state the length of the female urethra. A. Preprostatic 1 cm, prostatic 3 to 4 cm, membranous 1 to 2 cm, spongy 15 cm, total 18 to 20 cm. The female urethra is about 4 cm.

topics.topic: Urinary bladder: relations and support of the bladder neck
topics.male_form: The base of the bladder rests on the prostate. Posteriorly it is related to the seminal vesicles, the terminal parts of the deferent ducts and, through the rectovesical septum of Denonvilliers, to the rectum. The neck is anchored by the puboprostatic ligaments. The prostate provides a solid inferior support.
topics.female_form: There is no prostate. The bladder neck rests directly on the pelvic fascia and the anterior vaginal wall, and the base is related to the supravaginal cervix and the vagina. The neck is anchored by the pubovesical ligaments and the pubocervical fascia. Bladder capacity is functionally reduced in pregnancy by uterine pressure.
topics.why_examined: Bladder relations are a standard long answer, and examiners routinely ask what lies below the bladder in each sex.
topics.clinical: Loss of anterior vaginal wall support produces cystocele and stress urinary incontinence, treated by mid urethral sling. In the male the equivalent problem is bladder outflow obstruction from benign prostatic hyperplasia. Radical prostatectomy divides the puboprostatic ligaments and risks the continence mechanism.
topics.exam_q: Q. What supports the neck of the bladder in each sex? A. In the male, the prostate and the puboprostatic ligaments. In the female, the pubovesical ligaments, the pubocervical fascia and the anterior vaginal wall, with no prostate below the bladder.

topics.topic: Peritoneal pouches of the pelvis
topics.male_form: There is a single pouch, the rectovesical pouch, between the rectum and the bladder. It is the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in the male and lies about 7.5 cm above the anus, so it is within reach of the examining finger through the rectum.
topics.female_form: Two pouches, because the uterus intervenes. The vesicouterine pouch lies in front of the uterus and the rectouterine pouch, the pouch of Douglas, lies behind it. The pouch of Douglas is the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in the female and is separated from the posterior vaginal fornix only by peritoneum and a little connective tissue.
topics.why_examined: Standard applied anatomy question in the pelvis and in abdominal surgery. The peritoneum is not modelled here, so this is taught by pinning the organs and describing the space between them.
topics.clinical: Pus, blood and malignant deposits gravitate to these pouches. Ruptured ectopic pregnancy fills the pouch of Douglas, which is why culdocentesis or posterior colpotomy through the posterior fornix drains it. Transrectal or transvaginal drainage of a pelvic abscess uses the same anatomy. Drop metastases from stomach cancer form the Blumer shelf, palpable per rectum in both sexes.
topics.exam_q: Q. Name the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in each sex and give one clinical use. A. Rectovesical pouch in the male, rectouterine pouch of Douglas in the female. The pouch of Douglas is drained or sampled through the posterior vaginal fornix, for example in ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

topics.topic: Terminal course of the ureter: crossed by the deferent duct or by the uterine artery
topics.male_form: As it runs forward on the lateral pelvic wall, the ureter is crossed superiorly and anteriorly by the deferent duct, which hooks over it from lateral to medial as it descends to the seminal vesicle. The ureter then passes under the seminal vesicle to enter the bladder base obliquely.
topics.female_form: In the base of the broad ligament the ureter is crossed superiorly by the uterine artery, about 2 cm lateral to the supravaginal part of the cervix, at roughly the level of the ischial spine. This is the water under the bridge relationship, with the ureter as the water and the artery as the bridge.
topics.why_examined: The most reliably asked ureter question in India and the Gulf, because it carries a hard clinical consequence. Both crossing structures exist in this model, so the comparison can be pinned directly.
topics.clinical: Ureteric injury complicates roughly 0.5 to 1.5 percent of hysterectomies, most often as the uterine artery is clamped at the cervix. Prevention is by ureterolysis and by clamping close to the cervix. In the male the equivalent risk is ureteric injury during radical prostatectomy or during ligation of the deferent duct.
topics.exam_q: Q. What crosses the ureter near its termination in each sex, and why does it matter? A. The deferent duct in the male and the uterine artery in the female, the latter about 2 cm lateral to the cervix. The female relationship, water under the bridge, explains ureteric injury at hysterectomy.

topics.topic: Anterior relations of the rectum and digital rectal examination
topics.male_form: Above the peritoneal reflection the rectum is related to the rectovesical pouch and coils of ileum and sigmoid. Below it, through the rectovesical septum, it is related to the base of the bladder, the terminal deferent ducts, the seminal vesicles and, most importantly, the prostate. The prostate is the structure felt anteriorly on rectal examination.
topics.female_form: Above the reflection the rectum is related to the pouch of Douglas and its contents. Below the reflection it is related directly to the posterior wall of the vagina. On rectal or vaginal examination the cervix is what is felt anteriorly, and the ovaries and adnexa can be palpated in the fornices.
topics.why_examined: Rectal relations are a certain long answer, and the examiner will always ask what is felt anteriorly per rectum in each sex.
topics.clinical: Digital rectal examination assesses prostate size, consistency and the median sulcus, hard and nodular in carcinoma. In the female the same examination assesses the cervix, the pouch of Douglas for nodularity in endometriosis, and cervical excitation tenderness. Rectovaginal fistula follows obstructed labour and unrepaired fourth degree tears, an injury with no male counterpart.
topics.exam_q: Q. Name the anterior relations of the rectum below the peritoneal reflection in both sexes. A. Male: bladder base, terminal deferent ducts, seminal vesicles and prostate, separated by the rectovesical septum. Female: the posterior wall of the vagina.

topics.topic: Branches of the internal iliac artery: the sex specific set
topics.male_form: Anterior division supplies the superior vesical from the patent proximal umbilical artery, the inferior vesical which also supplies the prostate and seminal vesicle, the artery to the ductus deferens, the middle rectal, the obturator, the internal pudendal and the inferior gluteal. Posterior division gives iliolumbar, lateral sacral and superior gluteal in both sexes.
topics.female_form: The uterine artery and the vaginal artery take the place of the inferior vesical artery and the artery to the ductus deferens. The uterine artery is large, tortuous and crosses above the ureter. The ovarian supply is additionally received from the aorta, so the uterus has a double, anastomotic supply. The posterior division is identical to the male.
topics.why_examined: Internal iliac artery branches are a standard long answer, and the sex specific substitution is the discriminating detail examiners listen for.
topics.clinical: Internal iliac artery ligation is the classic operation for intractable postpartum haemorrhage. It works because pulse pressure falls while collateral flow from the ovarian, superior rectal and lumbar arteries preserves viability. Uterine artery embolisation for fibroids uses the same anatomy. In the male, the internal pudendal supply is the erectile blood supply damaged in pelvic fracture.
topics.exam_q: Q. Which branches of the internal iliac artery differ between the sexes? A. In the female the uterine and vaginal arteries replace the male inferior vesical artery and the artery to the ductus deferens. All other branches, including the posterior division, are the same.

topics.topic: External genital homologues
topics.male_form: Genital tubercle becomes the glans penis and the corpora cavernosa. The urogenital folds fuse in the midline over the urethral plate to form the ventral shaft of the penis and the spongy urethra, leaving the penile raphe. The labioscrotal swellings fuse to form the scrotum, leaving the scrotal raphe. The corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra and expands as the bulb and the glans.
topics.female_form: The genital tubercle becomes the glans and body of the clitoris with paired corpora cavernosa and crura. The urogenital folds do not fuse and become the labia minora. The labioscrotal swellings do not fuse and become the labia majora. The male corpus spongiosum corresponds to the paired bulbs of the vestibule and the spongy tissue around the female urethra. The male scrotal raphe corresponds to the posterior commissure.
topics.why_examined: Embryology and applied anatomy question in first year, and the anatomical basis of disorders of sex development in paediatrics.
topics.clinical: Failure of the urogenital folds to fuse gives hypospadias, the commonest male genital anomaly at about one in 250 male births. Excess androgen in congenital adrenal hyperplasia virilises the female external genitalia, producing clitoromegaly and labioscrotal fusion. Escutcheon pattern differs: male diamond shaped extending to the umbilicus, female triangular with a horizontal upper border, and a female pattern in a male suggests hypogonadism or cirrhosis.
topics.exam_q: Q. Give the female homologue of the glans penis, the corpus spongiosum, the scrotum and the ventral shaft skin of the penis. A. Glans clitoris, bulbs of the vestibule with the periurethral spongy tissue, labia majora, and labia minora respectively.

topics.topic: Prostate and its female homologue, and the greater vestibular glands
topics.male_form: A fibromuscular glandular organ about 3 by 4 by 2 cm, weighing about 8 to 20 g, surrounding the prostatic urethra below the bladder neck. McNeal zones: peripheral zone, the site of about 70 percent of carcinomas and the part felt per rectum, transition zone, the site of benign hyperplasia, and central zone. Drains by 15 to 20 ducts into the prostatic sinuses. The bulbourethral glands of Cowper lie in the deep perineal pouch.
topics.female_form: There is no prostate. Its homologue is the set of paraurethral or Skene glands opening beside the external urethral orifice, sometimes called the female prostate, and they are the source of Skene duct cysts and abscesses. The bulbourethral glands correspond to the greater vestibular glands of Bartholin, which lie in the superficial perineal pouch and are the site of Bartholin cyst and abscess.
topics.why_examined: Prostate is one of the highest yield structures in the whole syllabus. Examiners follow with the female homologue to test embryological understanding.
topics.clinical: Benign prostatic hyperplasia arises in the transition zone and obstructs the urethra. Carcinoma arises in the peripheral zone, which is why it is palpable late and detected by PSA and biopsy. Bartholin abscess is treated by marsupialisation. Skene gland infection is a differential for recurrent female urethral pain.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is the female homologue of the prostate and of the bulbourethral glands? A. The paraurethral or Skene glands correspond to the prostate, and the greater vestibular glands of Bartholin correspond to the bulbourethral glands of Cowper.

topics.topic: Pelvic venous plexuses and the vertebral venous plexus of Batson
topics.male_form: The prostatic venous plexus lies between the prostatic capsule and the fascial sheath, receives the deep dorsal vein of the penis and drains into the internal iliac veins and, through the sacral and lumbar veins, into the valveless internal vertebral venous plexus.
topics.female_form: The equivalent set is the uterovaginal plexus with the vesical and rectal plexuses, draining into the internal iliac veins and communicating with the same vertebral system. The ovarian veins add a second route, the left to the left renal vein and the right to the inferior vena cava. Pelvic venous engorgement in pregnancy and pelvic congestion syndrome have no male equivalent, although the male varicocele shares the left sided drainage logic.
topics.why_examined: Asked as applied anatomy in both anatomy and pathology, because it explains a pattern of metastasis that venous drainage to the lungs cannot explain.
topics.clinical: Batson plexus is valveless and pressure in it rises with coughing and straining, so tumour cells from the prostate in the male and the breast and pelvic organs in the female pass directly to vertebral and pelvic bones without traversing the lung. This explains osteoblastic vertebral secondaries in prostate cancer and the vertebral predilection of breast cancer secondaries.
topics.exam_q: Q. Explain how carcinoma of the prostate metastasises to the vertebral column without passing through the lungs. A. Through the prostatic venous plexus, which communicates with the valveless internal vertebral venous plexus of Batson via the sacral and lumbar veins, so tumour emboli bypass the caval and pulmonary circulation.

topics.topic: Gonadal vessels and the consequences of gonadal descent
topics.male_form: The testicular artery arises from the abdominal aorta just below the renal artery at about L2, reflecting the lumbar origin of the gonad, and runs a long retroperitoneal course over psoas and the ureter to reach the deep inguinal ring and the testis in the scrotum. The right testicular vein drains into the inferior vena cava at an acute angle, the left into the left renal vein at a right angle.
topics.female_form: The ovarian artery has an identical origin from the aorta at L2 but a much shorter course. It crosses the external iliac vessels at the pelvic brim and enters the suspensory ligament of the ovary to reach the ovary, which never leaves the abdomen. Venous drainage follows the same asymmetry, right ovarian vein to the inferior vena cava and left to the left renal vein.
topics.why_examined: The origin of the gonadal vessels at L2 and the asymmetric venous drainage are asked in almost every abdomen viva, with the varicocele question following immediately.
topics.clinical: About 90 percent of varicoceles are left sided, attributed to the right angled drainage into the left renal vein, its longer column of blood and possible compression in the nutcracker between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. A new right sided or non reducible varicocele demands imaging for a renal tumour. In the female, right ovarian vein thrombophlebitis is a recognised postpartum cause of fever, and left ovarian vein incompetence produces pelvic congestion syndrome.
topics.exam_q: Q. Why is varicocele commoner on the left, and what is the female counterpart of this drainage pattern? A. The left testicular vein enters the left renal vein at a right angle, has a longer column of blood and may be compressed between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery. The ovarian veins drain identically, left to left renal vein and right to inferior vena cava, giving left sided pelvic congestion syndrome.

topics.topic: Inguinal canal contents and the sex pattern of groin hernia
topics.male_form: The canal transmits the spermatic cord: the deferent duct, testicular artery, artery to the deferent duct, cremasteric artery, pampiniform plexus, lymphatics, sympathetic fibres and the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve, in three fascial coverings derived from the abdominal wall. The canal is larger, and the deep ring is a point of persistent weakness after testicular descent.
topics.female_form: The canal is narrower and transmits only the round ligament of the uterus, the developmental successor of the caudal gubernaculum, running to the labium majus, together with the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve and lymphatics. The processus vaginalis, if patent, is the canal of Nuck, which may form a cyst or an indirect hernia.
topics.why_examined: Inguinal canal is one of the most examined regions in the whole course, and the female content is the standard catch question.
topics.clinical: Inguinal hernia is far commoner in men, roughly seven to nine to one, because of the larger canal and testicular descent. Femoral hernia is commoner in women, roughly four to one, though inguinal hernia remains the commonest groin hernia even in women. Canal of Nuck hydrocele mimics an irreducible inguinal hernia in a girl. Indirect hernia passes lateral to the inferior epigastric artery, direct hernia medial to it.
topics.exam_q: Q. What are the contents of the inguinal canal in the female, and which hernia is relatively commoner in women? A. The round ligament of the uterus, the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve and lymphatics. Femoral hernia is relatively commoner in women, because of the wider femoral ring in the broader pelvis.

topics.topic: Femoral ring and femoral hernia
topics.male_form: The femoral ring is narrow. Its boundaries are the inguinal ligament in front, the pectineal ligament and superior pubic ramus behind, the sharp lacunar ligament medially and the femoral vein laterally. It is filled by the femoral septum and a lymph node of Cloquet. Femoral hernia is uncommon.
topics.female_form: The ring is relatively wider, because the pelvis is broader while the femoral vessels are of similar or smaller calibre, so the space medial to the vein is larger. Femoral hernia is therefore about four times commoner in women, and commoner still in the multiparous and the elderly.
topics.why_examined: Boundaries of the femoral ring are a certain viva item, and the sex difference is the applied follow up.
topics.clinical: Femoral hernia has a high risk of strangulation because the neck is narrow and the lacunar ligament medially is sharp and unyielding. It lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle, whereas an inguinal hernia lies above and medial. An abnormal obturator artery, present in about a quarter of people, may run on the lacunar ligament, historically the corona mortis, and is at risk during release of a strangulated sac.
topics.exam_q: Q. Give the boundaries of the femoral ring and explain why femoral hernia is commoner in women and prone to strangulation. A. Inguinal ligament in front, pectineal ligament behind, lacunar ligament medially, femoral vein laterally. The wider female pelvis widens the ring, and the sharp lacunar ligament with a narrow neck predisposes to strangulation.

topics.topic: Anterior abdominal wall in pregnancy: linea alba and diastasis recti
topics.male_form: The linea alba is narrow below the umbilicus and only a few millimetres wide there, wider above. The recti lie close together. Widening in the male is caused by obesity, ascites or repeated straining, not by physiological loading.
topics.female_form: In pregnancy the linea alba stretches and thins as the recti are displaced laterally, giving diastasis recti in a majority of women in the third trimester. Skin changes accompany it: linea nigra from increased melanocyte stimulating activity, and striae gravidarum. Most diastasis resolves within a year, some persists.
topics.why_examined: Rectus sheath and linea alba are core abdominal wall anatomy, and the pregnancy change is the applied anatomy that examiners use to test whether the student understands the wall as a dynamic structure. Note that rectus abdominis itself is absent from this model, so this is taught by pinning the linea alba and the external oblique.
topics.clinical: Diastasis weakens the wall, contributes to low back pain and gives an epigastric bulge on sitting up. Midline incisions in the pregnant or recently pregnant abdomen heal in a stretched aponeurosis and are more prone to incisional hernia. Divarication is not a hernia and does not need repair unless symptomatic.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is diastasis recti and why does it occur in pregnancy? A. Separation of the rectus muscles by stretching and thinning of the linea alba under the mechanical load of the enlarging uterus, seen in most women in the third trimester, usually resolving after delivery.

topics.topic: Position of the appendix in pregnancy
topics.male_form: The base of the appendix is constant at the confluence of the three taeniae on the caecum, surface marked at McBurney point, one third of the way along the line from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus. Position of the tip varies, retrocaecal in about 65 percent and pelvic in about 30 percent, but the base does not migrate.
topics.female_form: The same anatomy at rest, but from the second trimester the enlarging uterus displaces the caecum and appendix upwards and laterally, so pain and tenderness may present in the right flank or right upper quadrant near term. Modern imaging suggests the displacement is less consistent than the classical teaching of Baer claimed, and many appendices stay in the right lower quadrant.
topics.why_examined: Appendix is one of the most examined abdominal structures, and appendicitis in pregnancy is a standard applied anatomy and clinical question.
topics.clinical: Appendicitis is the commonest non obstetric surgical emergency in pregnancy, roughly one in 1500 pregnancies. Diagnosis is delayed because nausea and leucocytosis are physiological, the site of tenderness may be atypical, and the omentum is displaced so localisation is poorer, giving a higher perforation rate and fetal loss. Ultrasound first, then MRI, avoiding computed tomography.
topics.exam_q: Q. Why is appendicitis difficult to diagnose in late pregnancy? A. The gravid uterus may displace the caecum upwards so tenderness shifts towards the right flank or upper quadrant, physiological nausea and leucocytosis mask the picture, and the displaced omentum localises the inflammation poorly, so perforation is commoner.

topics.topic: Aortocaval compression in pregnancy
topics.male_form: The inferior vena cava lies on the right of the vertebral column, formed at L5 by the union of the common iliac veins, and is thin walled and easily compressed. Compression is caused by tumour, retroperitoneal mass or ascites, not by physiology.
topics.female_form: From about 20 weeks the gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava and, to a lesser degree, the aorta, when the woman lies supine. Venous return falls, cardiac output falls, and about 8 to 10 percent of women develop frank supine hypotensive syndrome with hypotension, pallor, nausea and syncope. Collateral return occurs through the vertebral venous plexus and the azygos system.
topics.why_examined: Applied anatomy of the inferior vena cava, asked in anatomy and again in obstetrics, anaesthesia and emergency medicine.
topics.clinical: Every pregnant woman beyond 20 weeks is nursed and resuscitated with a 15 to 30 degree left lateral tilt or manual left uterine displacement. In cardiac arrest in pregnancy, manual displacement is mandatory and perimortem caesarean within four minutes relieves the obstruction. The same compression contributes to leg oedema, varicose veins and haemorrhoids in pregnancy.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is supine hypotensive syndrome and how is it prevented? A. Compression of the inferior vena cava by the gravid uterus after about 20 weeks in the supine position, reducing venous return and cardiac output. It is prevented by a 15 to 30 degree left lateral tilt or manual left uterine displacement.

topics.topic: Physiological hydronephrosis of pregnancy
topics.male_form: The ureter is a 25 cm muscular tube with three constrictions: the pelviureteric junction, the crossing of the pelvic brim over the common iliac vessels, and the intramural segment at the bladder. Dilatation is always pathological and means obstruction.
topics.female_form: In pregnancy the ureters dilate above the pelvic brim in 80 to 90 percent of women, more on the right than the left. Two reasons are taught: mechanical compression at the brim by the dextrorotated uterus, with the left ureter partly cushioned by the sigmoid colon, and progesterone induced smooth muscle relaxation. Right sided dilatation may persist for several weeks after delivery.
topics.why_examined: Course and constrictions of the ureter are a certain long answer, and pregnancy dilatation is the applied anatomy that follows.
topics.clinical: Urinary stasis explains why asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy progresses to acute pyelonephritis in 20 to 30 percent if untreated, most often on the right, which is why every antenatal booking includes a urine culture. Physiological hydronephrosis must not be mistaken for obstructing calculus on ultrasound.
topics.exam_q: Q. Why does hydronephrosis of pregnancy affect the right side more? A. The uterus is dextrorotated and compresses the right ureter at the pelvic brim, while the left ureter is cushioned by the sigmoid colon. Progesterone induced smooth muscle relaxation adds to the dilatation.

topics.topic: Diaphragm and thoracic cage in pregnancy
topics.male_form: The dome of the diaphragm reaches the fifth intercostal space on the right and the fifth rib or space on the left in quiet expiration, and descends about 1.5 cm in quiet inspiration. The subcostal angle is approximately 70 degrees. Costal excursion is the major determinant of tidal volume alongside diaphragmatic descent.
topics.female_form: In pregnancy the diaphragm is elevated by up to about 4 cm, the subcostal angle widens from roughly 68 to over 100 degrees, and the transverse thoracic diameter increases by about 2 cm before the uterus is large enough to explain it, which points to a hormonal effect on ligaments. Tidal volume rises about 30 to 50 percent, functional residual capacity falls about 20 percent, and diaphragmatic excursion is preserved or increased.
topics.why_examined: Diaphragm is a guaranteed long answer, and its pregnancy behaviour is standard applied anatomy for anaesthesia and respiratory medicine.
topics.clinical: The reduced functional residual capacity with increased oxygen consumption is why pregnant women desaturate within seconds of apnoea, which governs rapid sequence induction and preoxygenation. Chest drains and needle decompression are placed one to two spaces higher than usual in late pregnancy because of the elevated diaphragm. Physiological dyspnoea of pregnancy affects most women and must be distinguished from pulmonary embolism.
topics.exam_q: Q. What happens to the diaphragm and the thoracic cage in pregnancy, and why does it matter in anaesthesia? A. The diaphragm rises up to 4 cm, the subcostal angle widens beyond 100 degrees and the transverse diameter increases. Functional residual capacity falls about 20 percent while oxygen consumption rises, so desaturation on apnoea is rapid.

topics.topic: Bed of the female breast on the male thorax
topics.male_form: The male breast is rudimentary, a small disc of duct tissue behind the areola with no lobules, resting on the same bed. The retromammary space and the fascial anatomy are identical, but the gland does not develop because it is not exposed to oestrogen and progesterone at puberty.
topics.female_form: A modified sweat gland lying in the superficial fascia, extending vertically from the second to the sixth rib and horizontally from the lateral sternal edge to the mid axillary line. Two thirds of the bed is pectoralis major, one third is serratus anterior and the aponeurosis of external oblique. The axillary tail of Spence pierces the deep fascia at the foramen of Langer. Arterial supply: perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery for about 60 percent, lateral thoracic and pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial for most of the rest, and posterior intercostals. About 75 percent of lymph drains to the axillary nodes, the rest largely to internal thoracic nodes.
topics.why_examined: The breast is one of the highest yield structures in the thorax and in surgery. Note that no breast tissue and no lymph nodes exist in this model, so this is taught by pinning the bed and the feeding arteries and describing the gland that lies upon them.
topics.clinical: Skin dimpling in carcinoma is traction on the suspensory ligaments of Cooper, and fixity to the chest wall is assessed by contracting pectoralis major. Medial quadrant tumours can spread to internal thoracic nodes and then to the opposite side or the mediastinum. Male breast cancer is about 1 percent of all breast cancer and presents late because the gland is thin and invades skin and chest wall early. Gynaecomastia in the male follows an oestrogen to androgen imbalance, seen in puberty, cirrhosis, spironolactone and digoxin.
topics.exam_q: Q. Describe the extent, the bed and the blood supply of the female breast. A. Second to sixth rib, sternal edge to mid axillary line. Bed is pectoralis major for two thirds, serratus anterior and external oblique aponeurosis for one third. Supply from internal thoracic perforators, lateral thoracic, pectoral branch of thoraco-acromial and posterior intercostal arteries.

topics.topic: Sternum: manubrium to body proportion in sex determination
topics.male_form: The body of the sternum is more than twice the length of the manubrium, and the total sternum is longer and broader. This is the classical statement known as Hyrtl law.
topics.female_form: The body of the sternum is less than twice the length of the manubrium, and the sternum overall is shorter and narrower. The sternal index, manubrium length over body length times 100, is higher in the female.
topics.why_examined: Standard forensic medicine question in Indian MBBS and a common osteology spot. It is one of the few post cranial, non pelvic sexing rules students are expected to name.
topics.clinical: Used in identification of skeletal remains when the pelvis and skull are missing. Accuracy is only moderate, roughly 80 percent in most series, so it is a supporting rather than a deciding trait. Sternal anatomy is also the basis of the sternal angle of Louis at the second costal cartilage, and of sternal marrow aspiration at the level of the second or third space.
topics.exam_q: Q. State Hyrtl law of the sternum and comment on its reliability. A. In the male the body of the sternum is more than twice the length of the manubrium, in the female less than twice. Accuracy is around 80 percent, so it supports but does not settle sex determination.

topics.topic: Coronary arteries and the sex difference in ischaemic heart disease
anchor_structures: trunk of anterior interventricular branch of coronary artery
topics.male_form: Epicardial coronary arteries are of larger calibre. Disease presents typically as obstructive atherosclerosis of the epicardial vessels, presenting a decade earlier, most often with classical exertional central chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw.
topics.female_form: Epicardial coronary calibre is smaller, only partly explained by body size. Presentation is later, protected until the menopause, and more often with dyspnoea, fatigue, nausea or epigastric discomfort rather than classical chest pain. Women have a higher proportion of myocardial infarction with non obstructive coronary arteries, and spontaneous coronary artery dissection, which is heavily female predominant and associated with the peripartum period and with fibromuscular dysplasia. Coronary microvascular dysfunction is commoner.
topics.why_examined: Coronary anatomy is a certain long answer, and the sex difference in presentation is examined in medicine and in clinical skills as a cause of missed diagnosis. The heart as a whole organ is absent from this model, so this is taught by pinning the coronary vessels and the great vessels.
topics.clinical: Women are more often misdiagnosed and treated later in acute coronary syndrome, and have worse outcomes after percutaneous intervention, partly attributable to smaller vessel calibre and to delay. Peripartum spontaneous coronary artery dissection is a recognised cause of infarction in a young woman with no atherosclerotic risk factors.
topics.exam_q: Q. How does the presentation of myocardial infarction differ in women, and name one female predominant coronary syndrome. A. More often dyspnoea, fatigue, nausea or epigastric pain rather than typical chest pain, leading to delayed diagnosis. Spontaneous coronary artery dissection is strongly female predominant and associated with the peripartum period.

topics.topic: Larynx: thyroid cartilage angle and vocal ligament length
topics.male_form: The two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet anteriorly at an angle of about 90 degrees, producing the prominent laryngeal prominence or Adam apple. The larynx enlarges markedly at puberty under androgen. Vocal ligament length is about 17 to 25 mm and fundamental frequency about 100 to 130 Hz.
topics.female_form: The laminae meet at about 120 degrees, so there is no visible prominence and the anterior neck contour is smooth. Vocal ligament length is about 12.5 to 17 mm and fundamental frequency about 200 to 230 Hz. Overall laryngeal dimensions are smaller in all planes.
topics.why_examined: The thyroid cartilage angle and the cord lengths are one of the very few numerically precise sex differences students are expected to quote, and the larynx is a guaranteed long answer.
topics.clinical: Landmarks for cricothyroidotomy are harder to palpate in women because the prominence is absent, so the cricothyroid membrane is identified by walking down from the hyoid or up from the sternal notch. Smaller female airway dimensions mean a smaller tracheal tube, usually 7.0 to 7.5 mm internal diameter versus 8.0 to 8.5 in men. Androgen exposure, therapeutic or from a virilising tumour, irreversibly lowers the voice by lengthening and thickening the cords.
topics.exam_q: Q. Give the angle between the thyroid laminae and the vocal ligament length in each sex. A. About 90 degrees and 17 to 25 mm in the male, about 120 degrees and 12.5 to 17 mm in the female, which is why the male voice is lower and the laryngeal prominence visible.

topics.topic: Sexing the cranium
topics.male_form: Heavier and thicker with rugged muscle markings. Glabella and supraorbital ridges prominent, supraorbital margin thick and rounded. Frontal bone sloping backwards. Mastoid process large, so the skull rests on the mastoids and the occipital condyles in the tripod test. External occipital protuberance and nuchal lines strongly marked. Zygomatic arch heavy and extending back past the external acoustic meatus. Palate large and U shaped. Cranial capacity around 1450 ml.
topics.female_form: Lighter and smoother with faint markings. Glabella and supraorbital ridges slight, supraorbital margin sharp. Frontal bone vertical with frontal and parietal bossing, retaining a more juvenile form. Mastoid small. Occipital markings faint and the occipital contour rounded. Zygomatic arch light. Palate smaller and more parabolic. Cranial capacity around 1300 ml, roughly 10 percent less, in proportion to body size.
topics.why_examined: Forensic medicine question in every Indian MBBS, and a common osteology spot in first year.
topics.clinical: Sex determination of unknown remains. Accuracy quoted in the standard forensic texts: pelvis alone about 95 percent, skull alone about 90 percent, pelvis with skull about 98 percent, long bones alone about 80 percent. Traits are population specific, so a robust female skull in one population may be misread against another population standard.
topics.exam_q: Q. List six cranial features that favour a male skull. A. Prominent glabella and supraorbital ridges, blunt rounded supraorbital margin, sloping frontal bone, large mastoid process, marked external occipital protuberance and nuchal lines, and a heavy zygomatic arch extending past the external acoustic meatus.

topics.topic: Sexing the mandible
topics.male_form: Larger and thicker overall. Chin square and often bilobed, the mental eminence prominent. Body longer and deeper at the symphysis. Ramus broader with a greater bigonial breadth, and the gonial region everted with rough masseteric markings. Gonial angle less obtuse, usually quoted as under about 125 degrees. Condyle larger.
topics.female_form: Smaller and lighter. Chin rounded or pointed with a less marked mental eminence. Ramus narrower, gonia not everted, surfaces smooth. Gonial angle more obtuse, usually quoted as over about 125 degrees. Condyle smaller.
topics.why_examined: The mandible is often described as the most sexually dimorphic single bone of the skull and is the commonest facial bone recovered intact, so it is a standing forensic question.
topics.clinical: Identification from fragmentary remains, and the same features underlie facial gender perception in reconstructive and gender affirming facial surgery. The gonial angle criterion has weak discriminating power in modern quantitative studies and should be quoted as a supporting trait, not a decisive one. The angle also widens with age and with loss of teeth in both sexes, which is a confounder that examiners like to probe.
topics.exam_q: Q. Give the mandibular features used for sex determination and state the main limitation. A. Square bilobed chin, deeper symphysis, broader ramus, everted gonia and a gonial angle under about 125 degrees favour a male. The limitation is that gonial angle also widens with age and edentulousness, so it discriminates weakly on its own.

topics.topic: Thyroid gland region: teaching an absent gland and its female preponderance
topics.male_form: The gland weighs about 25 g and lies with its lobes against the second to fourth tracheal rings, the isthmus crossing rings two to four, the upper pole limited by the attachment of sternothyroid to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage. Supply is the superior thyroid artery from the external carotid and the inferior thyroid artery from the thyrocervical trunk. Thyroid disease is much less common.
topics.female_form: Identical topography, but the gland is slightly larger and enlarges further in pregnancy and at puberty. Autoimmune thyroid disease is strongly female predominant, Hashimoto thyroiditis roughly seven to ten to one and Graves disease about five to ten to one. Thyroid nodules and differentiated thyroid carcinoma are about three times commoner in women, although the prognosis is worse in men.
topics.why_examined: The thyroid gland is a guaranteed long answer in head and neck. The gland itself is absent from this model, so it is taught by pinning the cartilages, the trachea and the inferior thyroid artery and describing what lies on them. That absence should be stated openly to the class rather than glossed over.
topics.clinical: A goitre moves on swallowing because the gland is bound to the larynx by the pretracheal fascia and the ligament of Berry. Thyroidectomy risks the recurrent laryngeal nerve, closely related to the inferior thyroid artery, and the external laryngeal nerve near the superior thyroid artery. Untreated maternal hypothyroidism impairs fetal neurodevelopment, which is why thyroid function is checked in pregnancy.
topics.exam_q: Q. State the extent and arterial supply of the thyroid gland and comment on the sex distribution of thyroid disease. A. Lobes lie against the second to fourth tracheal rings with the isthmus over rings two to four, supplied by the superior thyroid artery from the external carotid and the inferior thyroid artery from the thyrocervical trunk. Autoimmune thyroid disease and thyroid nodules are several times commoner in women.

topics.topic: Femur angles, the Q angle and knee injury risk
topics.male_form: Neck shaft angle about 125 degrees in the adult. The bicondylar or oblique angle of the femoral shaft to the vertical is smaller, about 11 to 12 degrees, because the acetabula are further apart relative to the knees. Quadriceps or Q angle is about 13 to 14 degrees. The intercondylar notch is wider.
topics.female_form: Neck shaft angle is slightly smaller. The wider pelvis with a shorter femur increases the bicondylar angle to about 14 to 15 degrees, so the femora converge more sharply to the knees, producing a physiological genu valgum. Q angle is about 17 to 18 degrees, and above 20 degrees is regarded as abnormal. The intercondylar notch is narrower and ligamentous laxity varies with the menstrual cycle.
topics.why_examined: The Q angle and the bicondylar angle are asked in lower limb applied anatomy and in orthopaedics, and they are the anatomical bridge from the wide female pelvis to knee pathology.
topics.clinical: The greater Q angle increases the lateral pull on the patella, contributing to patellofemoral pain syndrome and recurrent lateral patellar dislocation, both commoner in young women. Non contact anterior cruciate ligament rupture is roughly two to eight times commoner in female athletes, attributed to the greater valgus alignment, narrower intercondylar notch, quadriceps dominant landing pattern and hormonal laxity. Neuromuscular training programmes reduce that risk.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is the Q angle, how does it differ between the sexes and what is its clinical importance? A. The angle between the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the centre of the patella and the line from the patella to the tibial tuberosity, about 13 to 14 degrees in men and 17 to 18 in women. A greater angle increases lateral patellar pull and is linked to patellofemoral pain and to anterior cruciate ligament rupture.

topics.topic: Femoral head diameter and osteometric sexing of long bones
topics.male_form: Vertical diameter of the femoral head usually above about 47.5 mm, bicondylar breadth of the femur greater, and vertical diameter of the humeral head usually above about 47 mm. Long bones are longer and their articular ends and shafts more robust.
topics.female_form: Vertical diameter of the femoral head usually below about 42.5 mm, with an indeterminate band between the two cut off values. Humeral head vertical diameter usually below about 43 mm. Long bones are shorter and lighter, and regression formulae for stature from long bone length must use sex specific equations, so sex must be determined first.
topics.why_examined: Standard forensic medicine and osteology examination material, and the practical answer when a student is asked what to do when only limb bones are recovered.
topics.clinical: Skeletal identification when the pelvis and skull are missing. Accuracy of long bone metrics alone is around 80 percent, well below the pelvis. All cut off values are population specific, so Indian and Gulf population standards differ from the European series in which many of these values were derived, and this must be stated when the numbers are quoted.
topics.exam_q: Q. If only a femur is available, how would you determine sex and stature? A. Measure the vertical diameter of the head, above about 47.5 mm suggesting male and below about 42.5 mm female, together with bicondylar breadth, then apply a population specific and sex specific regression formula to the maximum length to estimate stature.

topics.topic: Carrying angle at the elbow
topics.male_form: With the elbow extended and the forearm supinated, the forearm deviates laterally from the arm by roughly 11 to 14 degrees. The angle disappears on flexion and on pronation, so the hand can reach the mouth.
topics.female_form: The angle is generally quoted as several degrees greater, roughly 13 to 17 degrees, attributed to a deeper trochlear notch and greater medial trochlear projection. The difference is small, overlaps widely between individuals, and several quantitative studies find it disappears when body size is controlled, so it should be taught as a tendency rather than as a rule.
topics.why_examined: Guaranteed viva item in upper limb osteology and in orthopaedics, invariably followed by cubitus valgus and varus.
topics.clinical: Increase of the angle is cubitus valgus, classically following non union of a lateral condylar fracture, and it causes tardy ulnar nerve palsy by stretching the nerve over years. Decrease is cubitus varus or gunstock deformity, classically after malunion of a supracondylar fracture. The angle is also increased in Turner syndrome, one of the few situations where an abnormal carrying angle is itself a diagnostic clue in a phenotypic female.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is the carrying angle, how does it differ in the sexes, and name two abnormalities. A. Lateral deviation of the extended supinated forearm from the arm, about 11 to 14 degrees in men and slightly more in women. Increase is cubitus valgus, which can cause tardy ulnar nerve palsy, and decrease is cubitus varus or gunstock deformity.

topics.topic: Lumbar lordosis and the lumbosacral junction
anchor_structures: intervertebral disk of fifth lumbar vertebra
topics.male_form: Lumbar lordosis is produced mainly by dorsal wedging of two lower lumbar vertebrae and their discs. The lumbosacral angle is smaller and the centre of mass shift with anterior loading is less well compensated.
topics.female_form: Lordosis is greater and is distributed over three wedged lumbar vertebrae rather than two, with relatively larger and more dorsally oriented zygapophyseal joints, described as an adaptation to the forward shift of the centre of mass in pregnancy. Lumbosacral angle is greater. In late pregnancy lordosis increases further as the woman leans back to compensate for the uterus.
topics.why_examined: Curvatures of the vertebral column are a standard first year question, and pregnancy related lordosis is the applied anatomy that links it to a common clinical complaint.
topics.clinical: Low back pain affects roughly half to two thirds of pregnancies, driven by increased lordosis, relaxin mediated ligament laxity at the sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis, and altered muscle mechanics. Symphysis pubis dysfunction and sacroiliac joint pain follow the same laxity. Epidural and spinal anaesthesia in labour are performed with the lumbar spine flexed to reverse the lordosis and open the interlaminar space at L3 to L4 or L4 to L5.
topics.exam_q: Q. How does lumbar lordosis differ between the sexes and why does it matter in pregnancy? A. It is greater in the female and is distributed over three wedged lumbar vertebrae rather than two, an adaptation to the shifted centre of mass. It increases further in pregnancy and contributes to the low back pain reported by most pregnant women.

topics.topic: Brain size and the corpus callosum: an honest card
topics.male_form: Average adult brain weight around 1350 to 1400 g and total intracranial volume roughly 10 to 12 percent greater than in the female. Absolute white matter volume and absolute corpus callosum cross sectional area are larger.
topics.female_form: Average adult brain weight around 1200 to 1250 g. Once total brain volume is controlled for, the female corpus callosum is proportionally similar or slightly larger, grey to white matter ratio is slightly higher, and regional differences shrink markedly. The widely repeated claim of a larger female splenium comes from a small 1982 study and has not been reliably replicated. There is no established anatomical basis in the human corpus callosum for claims about sex differences in cognition.
topics.why_examined: Asked as a factual comparison in neuroanatomy, and worth teaching precisely because the popular version of the answer is wrong. Teaching it correctly protects the professor and the students from repeating a claim that does not survive scrutiny.
topics.clinical: Brain volume is used as a covariate in imaging studies and in the interpretation of atrophy on scans, so sex specific normative data matter. Callosal agenesis, callosal infarction and Marchiafava Bignami disease are the pathologies of this structure, none of them sex specific.
topics.exam_q: Q. State the difference in brain size between the sexes and comment on the corpus callosum. A. Male brain volume is about 10 to 12 percent greater, in proportion to body size. Absolute callosal area is larger in the male, but after correcting for total brain volume there is no reliably replicated sex difference in the corpus callosum and no basis for inferring cognitive differences from it.

topics.topic: Hypothalamo-pituitary axis: cyclical versus tonic gonadotrophin release
topics.male_form: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone is secreted in a pulsatile but tonic pattern, driving steady luteinising and follicle stimulating hormone output and continuous spermatogenesis. Oestrogen exerts only negative feedback. The third interstitial nucleus of the anterior hypothalamus and the sexually dimorphic preoptic region are reported to be larger in males. The gland weighs about 500 mg and does not change in adult life.
topics.female_form: The same pulsatile generator, but in addition a capacity for oestrogen driven positive feedback, so that rising oestradiol from a mature follicle triggers the mid cycle luteinising hormone surge and ovulation. In pregnancy the gland enlarges by about a third from lactotroph hyperplasia, outgrowing its blood supply. The optic chiasm relationship is identical in both sexes.
topics.why_examined: The neural control of the menstrual cycle is examined in physiology and in obstetrics, and the pituitary fossa relations are examined in neuroanatomy. The comparison is what makes the cycle make anatomical sense.
topics.clinical: Sheehan syndrome is infarction of the enlarged pituitary after postpartum haemorrhage, presenting with failure of lactation, then amenorrhoea and panhypopituitarism, with no male counterpart. Prolactinoma presents early as a microadenoma in women through amenorrhoea and galactorrhoea, and late as a macroadenoma with bitemporal hemianopia in men because early symptoms are silent. Compression of the chiasm gives bitemporal hemianopia in either sex.
topics.exam_q: Q. What is Sheehan syndrome and why does it occur only in women? A. Ischaemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary following postpartum haemorrhage. The gland is enlarged by lactotroph hyperplasia in pregnancy and outgrows its portal blood supply, so it is vulnerable to hypotension, giving failure of lactation followed by panhypopituitarism.

topics.topic: Ischial spine as the landmark of the female perineum
topics.male_form: The ischial spine gives attachment to the sacrospinous ligament, separates the greater from the lesser sciatic foramen, and is the point at which the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels leave the pelvis, hook around the ligament and re-enter through the lesser foramen into the pudendal canal. It is prominent and inverted, and is palpable only per rectum.
topics.female_form: The same anatomy, but the spine is everted and less prominent, and is readily palpable per vaginam. It is therefore usable as a working clinical landmark, which is what makes the female spine a taught landmark and the male spine only an anatomical one.
topics.why_examined: The pudendal nerve is not present anywhere in this model, so this topic is deliberately anchored to the bone and the muscles that are. It is a standard obstetric anatomy question and rewards a student who can reason from bone to nerve.
topics.clinical: Transvaginal pudendal nerve block: the ischial spine is palpated, the needle is passed just medial and inferior to it through the sacrospinous ligament, and about 10 ml of local anaesthetic is deposited on each side, anaesthetising the S2 to S4 territory for outlet forceps delivery and perineal repair. The spine also gives fetal station zero and anchors sacrospinous fixation for vault prolapse.
topics.exam_q: Q. Describe the transvaginal pudendal nerve block and the anatomy on which it depends. A. The ischial spine is palpated vaginally, the needle passed just medial and inferior to it through the sacrospinous ligament where the pudendal nerve, roots S2 to S4, hooks around the ligament to enter the lesser sciatic foramen, and local anaesthetic is injected bilaterally.

topics.topic: Gallbladder and the female preponderance of gallstones
topics.male_form: Identical anatomy: fundus at the tip of the ninth costal cartilage where the lateral border of the rectus sheath crosses the costal margin, body, neck and the spiral valve of Heister in the cystic duct, Calot triangle bounded by the cystic duct, common hepatic duct and the liver, containing the cystic artery. Stones occur but at roughly half the rate.
topics.female_form: Same anatomy. Prevalence of gallstones is roughly twice that in men. Oestrogen increases hepatic cholesterol secretion and biliary cholesterol saturation, and progesterone reduces gallbladder motility, so pregnancy, parity and the oral contraceptive pill all raise risk. This is the basis of the traditional fat, forty, female, fertile teaching aid, which is a memory hook rather than a diagnostic rule.
topics.why_examined: Extrahepatic biliary apparatus is a certain long answer, and the sex distribution of gallstones is examined in surgery and in pathology.
topics.clinical: Symptomatic gallstones are the commonest indication for cholecystectomy. Biliary colic in pregnancy is common and laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the second trimester is the preferred timing when surgery is needed. Murphy sign, referred right shoulder tip pain via the phrenic nerve C3 to C5, and the risk to an aberrant right hepatic artery in Calot triangle are the standard applied points.
topics.exam_q: Q. Why are gallstones commoner in women, and give the boundaries of Calot triangle. A. Oestrogen increases biliary cholesterol saturation and progesterone reduces gallbladder emptying, so prevalence is about twice that of men and rises with pregnancy and parity. Calot triangle is bounded by the cystic duct, the common hepatic duct and the inferior surface of the liver, and contains the cystic artery.

sexdiff.honest_limits:
Comparative text is not a female model, and no amount of authored content changes that. Say this to buyers in the first meeting, not the third.

WHAT THIS MODULE HONESTLY DELIVERS
1. Every topic here is anchored to structures verified present in derived.json. I checked each anchor name programmatically against entities[].k, so nothing in the anchor lists is invented.
2. The teaching act is real: the professor pins a structure the student can rotate, section and isolate, then reads the comparative text off the card. For roughly 60 percent of these topics, notably the pelvis, urethra, ureter, internal iliac artery, inguinal canal and all the forensic sexing cards, the male structure IS the object of study and the female difference is genuinely a verbal comparison even in Gray's and Chaurasia. For those, text plus a male mesh is close to the full teaching value.
3. The module covers the exam surface. Sex differences in gross anatomy are examined overwhelmingly as tabulated comparisons and viva questions, not as image identification, and 36 authored comparisons cover essentially all of it for MBBS and Gulf equivalents.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO
1. It cannot show a single female structure. Uterus, ovary, uterine tube, vagina, broad ligament, round ligament, uterine artery, clitoris, labia, bulb of vestibule and the female urethra are all absent. Where the card says "the female form is", the student sees nothing new on screen. A student cannot identify the pouch of Douglas in a spotter station because it is not there.
2. It cannot support a female spotter examination, a female sectional anatomy exercise, or any assessment item that requires the student to point at female geometry. The 614 existing spotter stations remain male only.
3. Several anchors are coarser than the teaching needs. The hip bone is a single fused mesh piece, so the ilium, ischium and pubis are not separately selectable and the pubic symphysis, ischial spine, ischial tuberosity, acetabular rim and greater sciatic notch can only be pointed at as surface features of one object, not isolated or measured as named parts. The Phenice traits and the subpubic angle are therefore demonstrated by rotating the hip bone, not by selecting the pubis.
4. The coccyx does not exist in this mesh. I searched all 2,234 mesh pieces: there is a sacrum and no coccyx. The coccyx appears in the authored card text only. Any card involving coccygeal retropulsion in labour, the sacrococcygeal joint or the anococcygeal ligament is taught against the sacrum with an explicit statement that the coccyx is missing.
5. Other absences hit specific cards: no peritoneum, so the rectovesical and rectouterine pouches are taught as the space between two pinned organs; no perineal body, no bulbospongiosus, no ischiocavernosus, no deep transverse perineal muscle, so the perineum card anchors on the external anal sphincter and levator ani only; no breast, no lymph nodes, so the breast card teaches the bed and the arteries and describes the gland; no heart as a whole organ and no thyroid gland, so those cards teach around a hole and should say so aloud; no peripheral nerves at all, so the pudendal nerve, which is the entire point of the ischial spine card, is described and never shown.
6. Confidence is not uniform. I marked 20 topics high, 16 medium, none low. Medium means either the numeric values vary between standard texts and populations (sacral index, acetabular diameter, gonial angle, carrying angle, femoral head cut offs, cranial capacity), or the claim rests on a specific study I am recalling rather than a settled textbook fact (three wedged lumbar vertebrae in women, sexually dimorphic hypothalamic nuclei), or modern evidence has weakened the classical teaching (appendix displacement in pregnancy, corpus callosum dimorphism, gonial angle discrimination). I did not verify any of this against a live source in this session: I had no network access and worked from memory of Gray's, Chaurasia, Cunningham's and Snell's. Every medium card should be checked against a current edition before a professor reads it to 150 students, and the forensic cut off values should be replaced with Indian and Gulf population standards where those exist, because most published cut offs derive from European skeletal series.

COMMERCIAL HONESTY
This module is worth building because it is fast, cheap, defensible and it makes the male mesh teach more than it currently does. It is not a substitute for female geometry and should never be sold as one. The correct positioning is: complete comparative sex differences content, taught against a male model, with the female model on the roadmap. A buyer who is told that up front will accept it. A buyer who discovers it in month two will not.
